zh:
小莲不知道，丁香到底是大侠，还是神仙。
别看她每天都笑呵呵的，可她懂得事情好多。燕北的白雪，塞外的驼铃，江南的柔波，西蜀的险峻……
小莲不知道，丁香到底是从哪来的。
虽然她有时候有点聒噪，还总有一些稀奇古怪的想法。但小莲知道，只要跟紧了这个姑娘，她就总有一口饭吃，一地安寝。
可慢慢地，丁香同她讲的故事越变越少。那些传说和远方的风景，掺进了许多不能言说的秘密。
这个曾经能拉着她说一晚上故事的姑娘，变成了燕北盟藏着最多心事的人。
直到有一天，丁香的脸上又恢复了以往兴奋的神色。小莲看着她一边叽里呱啦地讲一些她从未听过的故事，一边手忙脚乱地给不同的人写不同的信。
小莲不识字，只知道那些信鸽衔着信，往四面八方飞了去。
她听见丁香神秘兮兮地说，自己知道了一个天大的秘密，可惜，不能告诉任何人
“我要悄悄地跑到将军身边去，好好地同他说上一回——”
“瞧，如今我什么都知道了！”
小莲不知道，什么是大秘密，将军又是谁。
但她记住了丁香的神情——
那是一种蒙恩已久、终可报答的快意；更是一腔侠义，牵动风云的激昂。
en:
Xiao Lian never knew whether Ding Xiang was a hero or a goddess.
For all her daily smiles, the girl seemed to know so much: the white snows of the north, the camel bells beyond the frontier, the gentle waters of Jiangnan, the sheer peaks of Xishu... Xiao Lian never knew where she had come from.
She could be a chatterbox, always full of strange notions. But Xiao Lian knew that so long as she kept close to this girl, there would always be a meal to eat and a safe patch of ground to sleep on.
Yet little by little, Ding Xiang's stories grew fewer. Those legends and far-off scenes came laced with secrets that could not be spoken. The girl who once spun tales the whole night through became the one who carried more upon her heart than anyone in the Northern Vow.
Then one day, the old excitement lit her face again. Xiao Lian watched her rattle off stories she had never heard before, all while scrambling to write letter after letter, each for someone different.
Xiao Lian could not read. She only knew that carrier pigeons bore those letters off in every direction.
She heard Ding Xiang whisper, all mystery, that she had learned a secret vast as the sky, one she could tell to no one.
"I'll slip away to the general's side, and have a proper word with him at last."
"See? Now I know everything!"
Xiao Lian did not know what the great secret was, nor who the general might be.
But she never forgot the look on Ding Xiang's face. It was the joy of one who, long in another's debt, could at last repay it; and more than that, a heart brimming with valor, poised to turn the tides of the age.

朝九的手指头的肉又被削掉了一块，但他开心得很。
这次发百针而百中。他的流霰针，算是练成了。
他大摇大摆地离开家，打听哪里是这江湖中英雄最多的地方。
谁敢再嘲笑他，他就杀了谁。

被强绑着离开大营的时候，朝九骂了一路，他要让这群有眼无珠的人尝尝流霰针的厉害，要让他们给自己舔靴子。
但最后给他松绑的人，按住了他。
这个用刀的老头说，认得早就失传的流霰针。
这是要几十年吃饭都在动手，是要把手指头差点削成白骨，才能练成的功夫。
这是一门，好功夫。

朝九的流霰针第一次现身江湖，就在中渡桥边。
每一根都精准地扎在了契丹人的要害。
他大笑着喊，虏狗！见识下你爷爷的绝世好功夫！
鸿飞刀和他背靠着背，战到最后一刻。

暗器用光了，朝九捡起地上的刀，按照刚学的，继续杀着眼前的敌人。
老头子就是不中用，又比他先死，跟他那没用的爹一样。
但老头子是个识货的，他说能守住，就一定能守住。
他们两个人，就能守住中渡桥，能让那些人平安过桥去。

而他们会死在桥这头，流霰针也会江湖无名。
但朝九开心得很，他乐意。
en:
Another piece of flesh was sliced from Zhao Jiu's finger, but he was delighted.
A hundred needles thrown, a hundred hits. His Laid Bare Needles were finally perfected.
He swaggered away from home, asking where the most heroes in the Jianghu gathered.
He would kill anyone who dared to mock him.

Bound and forced from the camp, Zhao Jiu cursed the whole way. He wanted these blind fools to taste his Laid Bare Needles and lick his boots.
But the one who finally untied him held him down.
This old man with a blade said he recognized the long-lost Laid Bare Needles.
It was a skill perfected only by decades of practice, working until the fingers were nearly worn to the bone.
It is a fine skill.

Zhao Jiu's Laid Bare Needles first appeared at Zhongdu Bridge.
Every needle struck the Khitans' vitals with precision.
He laughed and shouted, "Khitan dogs! Witness my peerless skill!"
He fought with his Soaring Blade until the very end.

Out of hidden weapons, Zhao Jiu picked up a blade from the ground and continued to kill the enemies as he had just learned.
The old man was useless, dying before him just like his worthless father.
But the old man knew his craft; he said if they could hold, they would hold.
The two of them alone could hold Zhongdu Bridge and let the others cross safely.

They would die on this side of the bridge, and the Laid Bare Needles would remain nameless in the world.
But Zhao Jiu was delighted. He was willing.

zh: 元和四年秋，闻狱中夜有嚎哭者，听其音，不似长安之声。问其人，身出陇右，本为官身，驻于悬泉驿中。蕃戎侵扰，交通断绝。辞别朋友，孤身赶赴长安。中途没于戎人之手，改服易音，#Y信物皆失#E，茹毛饮血数十余年。一朝得机，藏青冢寒草，历黄河薄冰，昼伏宵行，进入唐境，边军视为戎人擒缚。拜迎再三不可免，判流配江南卑湿地。言罢悯然，遂遣酒，使其暖身。余幼居边镇，知边将之拥兵不战，虚奏邀功。此番亲闻亲见，颇极愤慨，故与友人各作《缚戎人》之诗。
en:
One autumn night in the capital, I heard a man weeping in his cell. His cries spoke of a home far from Chang'an. He told me his story. He was from Longyou, an officer at Celestial Spring Station. When the northern tribes swept through and cut the roads, he raced toward the capital alone.
But he was captured. For decades, he lived as a ghost of his former self—forced into foreign clothes and a foreign tongue, #Yall tokens of his identity lost#E. He lived as they did, a life of bitter hardship. At the first chance, he fled, surviving on nothing, crossing the frozen Yellow River, until he finally reached the Tang border. There, our own soldiers seized him, branding him a spy. His desperate pleas meant nothing. His sentence: exile to the humid south.
A silence fell as he spoke. My heart ached for him, and I called for wine to drive the chill from his bones. I know the frontier. I know the generals who let their weapons rust while they invent victories on paper. His story brought that quiet anger to a boil. In response, a friend and I each wrote a poem: "The Man in Foreign Chains."

zh:
穿青衣的男人坐在正店的角落里。这里虽不及樊楼富丽堂皇，却胜在人气热闹。隔着一道屏风，邻桌的酒令划得震天响，唯独他这一桌，冷清得像是在另一个世道。
他点了几样江南的小菜，一道清汤鱼圆，一道酒糟鸭信。他本是中原人，可在那烟雨迷蒙的江南蛰伏太久，口味早就变了。如今吃不得太咸太重，只喜清淡。其实也不是喜淡，而是这舌头早就麻木了。
做暗探的人，心是悬着的，舌头是僵的。终日绷着一根弦的琴，弹不出好听的曲子，自然也尝不出饭菜的滋味。
这开封厨子做的鱼圆，其实并不地道。江南讲究的是“鱼肉如雪，汤清如水”，这里的鱼圆多了几分面粉气，汤里也透着股葱姜的躁意。说来也好笑，江南那些寻常不过的做法，离了那方水土，便怎么也仿不像了。 
原来这世上，最难得的，往往就是那一点“寻常”。 
如今弦断了，不用再做那些偷听窥视的勾当，耳朵却落下了毛病。哪怕隔着屏风，邻桌男人的闲话还是直往耳朵里钻：哪家的蒙童逃了学被先生打了手板，瓦子里的美人换了新曲，大相国寺门口有人拿尿壶当古董骗了外乡人…… 
嘴碎，絮叨，穷极无聊，可他听得津津有味。伴着这些市井废话，那碗不地道的鱼圆，竟也让他吃出了一点滋味。 
做人大概就是这样没意思吧。翻来覆去说着前人说过的话，南辕北辙地忙活些琐碎的事。但这就是日子。寻常人寻常生，热气腾腾的寻常日子。  

“好了，不喝了！我家娃儿放学了，晚了婆娘要骂。”
隔壁一阵哄笑，那男人扔下铜板，急匆匆地走了。 
笑声远去，他转头望向窗外熙攘的长街。那样寻常的日子，在他记忆里已经模糊得像上辈子的事了。他也记不清家里人是不是也曾这样急着来接他放学。  
按理说他早该死了。要么死在醉花阴那杯毒酒里，要么死在韩家灭门那夜的尸堆下，要么死在闯宫时禁军随手的一刀中。能活到今天坐在这里吃鱼圆，本身就是一件极不寻常的事。
既是早该死的鬼，就不该独自赖在这寻常间。 
盘中菜已尽，杯中酒已干，该上路了。有个计策他盘算了许久，没什么用，但至少对得起韩家。站起身，理了理衣襟，他轻声哼起那首他自己谱的《玉京春慢》。 曲调悠扬，混在嘈杂的叫卖声里，没人听见。他就这样哼着曲子，踱步出门，走到久别重逢的死亡里去了。
en:
A man in a blue robe sat alone in the corner of a tavern. It lacked Revelry Hall's gilded grandeur, but it made up for that in bustle. Beyond a folding screen, the next table erupted in loud drinking games; his own table, by contrast, felt as if it belonged to another world.
He ordered a few simple Jiangnan dishes: clear-broth fish balls and duck tongues cured in wine lees. A native of the Central Plains, he'd lain low in the misty Jiangnan long enough for his palate to change.
Now he craved only the light and the plain. Not that he truly preferred blandness; his tongue had simply gone numb.
Spying had left him taut-hearted and tongue-locked. A string stretched too tight will never yield a sweet note, and naturally, one can taste no flavor in their food.
The Kaifeng cook's fish balls were, in truth, not quite authentic. Jiangnan values "fish as white as snow, broth as clear as water," but here the fish balls carried a floury texture, and the soup held a restless hint of scallion and ginger. It was almost comic that those most ordinary Jiangnan ways of cooking simply cannot be replicated once they leave that specific climate and soil.
It turns out that what is most rare in this world is often just a touch of the "ordinary."
Now that his string had snapped and he no longer needed to engage in the dirty work of eavesdropping, his ears had retained their old afflictions. Even through the screen, the neighboring table's idle chatter still bored straight into his ears: a schoolboy getting his palms caned by the teacher for skipping class, a courtesan trying a new tune, an out-of-towner duped by a chamber pot passed off as an antique at the gates of the Grand Imperial Temple...
Petty, gossipy, utterly trivial, yet he listened with great relish. Accompanied by this mundane street gossip, that bowl of unauthentic fish balls actually yielded a hint of flavor.
Perhaps this is what it means to be human: to repeat what has been said before, to busy oneself with small, pointless tasks. And yet those are life, steaming and alive with the warmth of the commonplace.

"Alright, no more drinking! My little one's out of school, and my wife will scold me if I'm late."
The neighboring table erupted in laughter; the man tossed down a few copper coins and hurried away.
As the laughter faded, he turned toward the window, looking out at the bustling street. Such ordinary days had long since blurred in his memory, as if belonging to another life. He could not even remember whether anyone in his own family had once rushed to pick him up from school like that.
By all rights, he should have been killed long ago. Killed by that cup of poisoned wine at Velvet Shade. Killed beneath the heap of corpses the night the Han family was massacred. Killed by a casual slash of an imperial guard's blade when he stormed the palace. To still be alive today, sitting here feasting on fish balls, was in itself a highly extraordinary thing.
Since he was a ghost who should have died long ago, he had no business lingering alone in this world of the ordinary.
The food on his plate was gone, the wine in his cup drained dry; it was time to be on his way. He had been plotting a scheme for a long time; it might be of little use, but at least it would do justice to the Han family.
He rose, smoothed his robes, and softly hummed the tune he had composed himself, "Spring in the Capital." The melody was melodious, lost amidst the clamorous cries of street vendors, heard by no one.
And so, humming the tune, he strolled out the door, stepping into a long-awaited reunion with death.

阿蒲原是一只流浪的小猫，它被冰葡萄的香气吸引至此。村里的人见它眼巴巴盯着，便摘下一颗葡萄放在手心里，它畏畏缩缩地舔上一口——那是它猫生中最甜美的味道。
可惜它已经许久没有再品尝过了。
如今夜半三分时，阿蒲常常能看到一些老面孔：给它洗澡的人、给它喂零食的人、还有那个第一次给它尝葡萄滋味的人。它曾试着叫醒村里已熟睡的人，可被吵醒后，他们全然看不见自己挂念的人就在面前。几次下来，阿蒲也放弃了。算啦，那自己就替他们多看看吧。
en:
Once a stray kitten, Grape was drawn here by the scent of frozen grapes. The villagers, seeing its hopeful eyes, offered a single grape. Timidly, Grape tasted it—the sweetest flavor it had ever known. 
But such sweetness had long since faded from its life. 
At midnight, Grape sees familiar faces—those who once cared for it. It tries to wake them, but they never see it. After many tries, Grape gave up and now quietly watches over them instead.

zh:
醉花阴中从不缺欢喜和忧愁，定下群英会登台名录的前后几日尤其如此。花信风们对这些儿女心思往往只会置之一哂，但好脾气的弱兰不同，她总是愿意与人开解。便如这一晚，她就在云华楼西侧的池塘边，邂逅了一位起舞弄清影姑娘。她只是站在银白色的月光里静静地瞧，反倒是姑娘猛然见了她，被吓了一跳。
“是我的错。”弱兰打断了姑娘的行礼，“你好好练，祝你在试艺中得偿所愿。”
弱兰的鼓励和她笑容一样，又真诚又温柔。可姑娘听了，却忽得落下泪来。
原来，她早就猜到了落选的结局。怎能猜不到呢？这次群英会的主题是飞天舞，可她在舞蹈上天赋平平，同门一次便能学会的舞姿，她总要多练个好几次才能做到。
姑娘哭着对弱兰说完了这数月来的委屈。她并不指望弱兰会因为她的眼泪便让自己破格入选，但此时此刻，哪怕是几句“勤能补拙”的谎言，也会让自己觉得好受一些。可是在认真听完姑娘的说辞之后，弱兰却露出几分讶异的神情。
“怎么，你要比试舞蹈而非唱歌？亏我跟着你的歌声寻了一路呢！”
这明显不是姑娘期待中的回答。她微微一愣，不自觉得就停下了流泪。弱兰见她似懂非懂，又用她一贯平和而温柔的语调继续说道。
“舞乐相和，缺一不可。你的歌声，很好听。”
姑娘若有所思地想了想。再抬头时，眼睛里的泪光褪去了，渐渐焕发出新的光彩。

弱兰是在姑娘的连番拜谢中施施然而去的。她缓步登上云华楼的沏香小阁，少见地打开最下层的衣柜，从那里翻出几件裙裾来。虽然那几条罗裙上的牡丹花样已经陈旧，但仍不难从其繁复的织工和连缀的珠玉上想象出它们曾经的金翠辉煌。
很难想象一贯低调谦和、只以芳草为饰的弱兰少年时居然曾偏爱过这样的衣裳。就像若不是今夜的相遇，可能连弱兰都忘了，她也曾执着于牡丹花笺的归属，也曾因师尊的选择而心生不甘与愤懑。可宋如烟是何种人，她一眼便看破了弱兰的心思。
“一枝独秀不成景，万紫千红才是春。”那朵已快凋谢的牡丹，也曾这般点拨过她的迷惘，“我希望的是，你们每个人都能成为我的骄傲。”
是啊，一百二十花朝日，二十四番花信风。谁能说幽兰定然不及牡丹娇艳？失了幽兰的牡丹，也会逊色非常。
弱兰看着眼前的几件旧衣，脸上再次浮现出那令人熟悉的温柔而安宁的微笑。她静静地合上衣柜，就像关上了一段过去的执着与迷惘。
en:
Velvet Shade has always been a place of joys and sorrows, none more so than in the days surrounding the finalization of the Heroes Assembly performance list. The Flowers often dismiss such petty worries with a scoff, but the gentle Ruo Lan is different. She always takes time to listen. One night, by the west pond of Nimbus Tower, she encountered a young woman dancing alone in the moonlight. Ruo Lan simply stood and watched in the silver light, but the girl started in surprise when she noticed her. "My fault," Ruo Lan interrupted the girl's bow. "Keep practicing, and may your wishes come true in the audition." Her encouragement was as sincere and soft as her smile. But the girl's eyes filled with tears.
She had already guessed she would fail. How could she not? The assembly's theme was the "Skyward Dance," and she lacked natural talent. While her peers mastered moves in one try, she needed countless repetitions.
Through tears, the girl poured out months of frustration. She didn't expect special treatment, just some comforting lie like "hard work beats talent." But after listening, Ruo Lan looked puzzled.
"Wait, you're auditioning for dance, not singing? I followed your voice all the way here!"
It was not the response the girl expected. She froze, tears drying mid-fall. Seeing her confusion, Ruo Lan continued gently, "Music and dance are two halves of the same coin. Your singing is lovely."
The girl pondered this. When she looked up again, the tears had vanished, replaced by a new light.

Amid the girl's grateful bows, Ruo Lan drifted away. She climbed to the Fragrance Pavilion of Nimbus Tower and retrieved several old dresses from a rarely opened bottom wardrobe. Though the peony patterns were faded, the intricate weaving and beaded jade trimmings hinted at their former splendor.
It was hard to imagine the modest Ruo Lan, who adorned herself with only simple fragrant herbs, had once loved such ornate clothes. Just as tonight's encounter had reminded her: she too had once obsessed over peony-themed invitations and once resented her master's choices. But Song Ruyan, like a wilting peony, had seen through her struggles.
"A single bloom does not make a spring. A thousand colors do," the older woman had chided her. "I want each of you to make me proud."
Yes, 120 days of floral beauty, 24 cycles of flower winds. Who says orchids cannot rival peonies? A peony without orchids is less vibrant.
Gazing at the old dresses, Ruo Lan smiled that familiar, serene smile. She closed the wardrobe, shutting away a past of obsession and doubt.

zh:
我与那位将军做了一笔交易，我为他提供粮食，他为我修造水井。
即便是长途迁徙的飞鸟，也会选择一处短暂的歇脚之地。
窣利商队选择的歇脚处，往往便是这样的有井之地。
可这一次，我歇的时间似乎有点久。或许是跟造井这样的工事费时弥久有关系。
起初，唐军只派了些人来修，他们还要守城，是以进度并不快。
跟我当初料想的一样，这笔交易其实不划算。
可不知从什么时候起，这里又多了许多乡民，他们帮着唐军修井，不为钱，不为利。
他们说不上什么理由，只是嚷着想回中原看看，想回长安看看。
长安。曾经我也很向往这城池，在父辈们传授的经商之道里，
那是成为大商主后，一路持节颂祷，才能去的土地。
可这些大多没去过长安的将士乡民，要到长安去的理由又是什么呢？
我问那位城楼上的将军，他说长安是他们国家的中心，也是他们心中的故里。
我不懂故里的含义，将军说有牵挂的地方就是故里，那个能让游子停下的地方，就是故里。
我未解其意，我问将军：如果亲自去一趟长安、是否会让我明白什么是故里？
将军摇了摇头：
会，但你不该去，不该现在去。
会，便该去。我笑着和将军谈起一笔新生意：你们不是一直想找个不受波陈怀疑的胡人，轻装潜行到长安传消息吗？我替你们去！
我倾身夺过马鞭，骑着他的白马，过三关奔万里。一路驱驰到了传说中的长安。
长安很好，但不知怎地，我却很想念那个跟将士、乡民一起待过的市集。
回来时，我看见曾住过的棚子里有星星点点的光明。
守门的小厮笑着招呼我，
“将军说啦，康商主不知何日归来，要留一盏灯才好哩。”
我这才明白，故乡原来就是这个样子。
蓦然间，我想把这里建得更大，更好。让胡杨扎根在此，生出万千金色枝条。
我想把我的“故乡”，建成窣利人的家乡。
en:
I struck a deal with the general: I provide the grain, and he builds the well.
Even migrating birds need a place to rest on their long journey. For the Sogdian caravans, these resting places are always found where there is water.
But this time, my stay has been longer than I intended—perhaps because digging a well is a slow and arduous task.
At first, the Tang army sent only a few men. They still had a city to guard, so progress was slow. Just as I'd calculated, it was not a profitable deal.
But then, villagers started to appear. They helped the soldiers, not for coin or for profit. They couldn't quite explain why, only murmuring about wanting to see the Central Plains, to see Chang'an again.
Chang'an. I once longed for that city myself. In the lessons of trade passed down from my elders, it was a land one could only travel to after becoming a great merchant, carrying credentials and chanting prayers.
But what reason did these soldiers and villagers have, most of whom had never even been there?
I asked the general as he stood on the city wall. He told me Chang'an is the heart of their country. Their homeland.
I didn't understand what "homeland" meant. "A homeland," he explained, "is where you have ties. It's the place that lets a wanderer stop wandering."
His meaning still eluded me. "If I go to Chang'an myself," I asked, "will I understand?"
He shook his head. "You would. But you shouldn't go. Not now."
"If I would understand, then I must go." I smiled, countering with a new business proposal. "You've been looking for a foreigner the Bodchen wouldn't suspect, someone to travel light and carry a message to Chang'an. Let me go for you!"
I leaned forward, snatched the whip from his hand, and set off on his white horse, crossing three passes and a thousand miles to reach the fabled city of Chang'an.
It was magnificent. But strangely, I found myself missing the simple market where I'd spent my days with the soldiers and villagers.
When I returned, I saw a small light flickering in the shelter where I had stayed.
The guard at the gate greeted me with a smile. "The general said your return was uncertain, Master Kang, so he ordered us to keep a lamp lit for you."
In that moment, I understood. This is what a homeland is.
Suddenly, I had a new dream: to build this place bigger, better. To let the desert poplars sink their roots here and grow a thousand golden branches.
I want to build my "homeland" into a true home for the Sogdian people.

zh:
【投壶第四十】

投壶之礼，主人奉矢，司射奉中，使人执壶。主人请曰：“某有枉矢哨壶，请以乐宾。”宾曰：“子有旨酒嘉肴，某既赐矣，又重以乐，敢辞。”主人曰：“枉矢哨壶，不足辞也，敢以请。”宾曰：“某既赐矣，又重以乐，敢固辞。”主人曰：“枉矢哨壶，不足辞也，敢固以请。”宾曰：“某固辞不得命，敢不敬从？”宾再拜受，主人般还，曰：“辟。”主人阼阶上拜送，宾般还，曰：“辟。”已拜，受矢，进即两楹间，退反位，揖宾就筵。
司射进度壶，间以二矢半，反位，设中，东面，执八算兴。
请宾曰：“顺投为入。比投不释，胜饮不胜者，正爵既行，请为胜者立马，一马从二马，三马既立，请庆多马。”请主人亦如之。
命弦者曰：“请奏《狸首》，间若一。”大师曰：“诺。”
左右告矢具，请拾投。有入者，则司射坐而释一算焉。宾党于右，主党于左。
卒投，司射执算曰：“左右卒投，请数。”二算为纯，一纯以取，一算为奇。遂以奇算告曰：“某贤于某若干纯”。奇则曰奇，钧则曰左右钧。
命酌曰：“请行觞。”酌者曰：“诺。”当饮者皆跪奉觞，曰：“赐灌”；胜者跪曰：“敬养”。
正爵既行，请立马。马各直其算。一马从二马，以庆。庆礼曰：“三马既备，请庆多马。”宾主皆曰：“诺。”正爵既行，请彻马。
……
en:
【Pitch Pot, Chapter 40】

In the ritual of Pitch Pot, the host presents the arrows, the master of ceremonies presents the tally stand, and an attendant carries the pot. The host says, "I have crooked arrows and a whistling pot, please allow me to entertain the guests with this game." The guest replies, "You have fine wine and excellent dishes; I have already been favored, and now to add this entertainment, I dare to decline." The host says, "Crooked arrows and a whistling pot are not worth declining; I dare to insist." The guest says, "I have already been favored, and now to add this entertainment, I dare to firmly decline." The host says, "Crooked arrows and a whistling pot are not worth declining; I dare to firmly insist." The guest says, "I have firmly declined but cannot refuse your command; dare I not respectfully comply?" The guest bows twice and receives the arrows, while the host turns away, saying, "Step aside." The host bows and sends off from the eastern steps, and the guest turns away, saying, "Step aside." After the bows, the guest receives the arrows, advances to stand between the two pillars, then retreats to his original position, and bows to invite the guests to their mats.
The master of ceremonies advances and sets up the pot, placing it at a distance of two and a half arrows, then returns to his position, sets up the tally stand, faces east, and picks up the eight counting sticks, rising.
He invites the guest, saying, "A straight throw counts as a score. Consecutive throws are not counted. The winner drinks to the loser. After the ceremonial cup has been passed, please set up a Horse for the winner; one Horse follows two Horses. When three Horses are set up, please celebrate the one with the most Horses." He invites the host in the same manner.
He commands the musicians, saying, "Please play 'Li Shou,' with even intervals." The Grand Master says, "Yes."
Those on the left and right announce that the arrows are ready and request to take turns throwing. When someone scores, the master of ceremonies sits and places one counting stick. The guest's party is on the right, and the host's party is on the left.
When the throwing is finished, the master of ceremonies holds the counting sticks and says, "The left and right have finished throwing; please count." Two sticks form a pair, and pairs are taken together; one stick is an odd. He then announces with the odd count, saying, "So-and-so surpasses so-and-so by so many pairs." If there is an odd, he says "odd"; if equal, he says "left and right are equal."
He commands the pourer, saying, "Please pass the cups." The pourer says, "Yes." Those who should drink all kneel and hold up their cups, saying, "Grant us the drink"; the winners kneel and say, "Respectfully nourish."
After the ceremonial cup has been passed, please set up the Horses. Each Horse corresponds to its counting stick. One Horse follows two Horses, to celebrate. The celebration ritual says: "Three Horses are complete; please celebrate the one with the most Horses." Both the guest and host say, "Yes." After the ceremonial cup has been passed, please remove the Horses.
……

自坎尔孜往南，见一绿洲，郁郁葱葱。行近，风沙蔽目。再向内探，热气蒸腾，绿洲消散无影，只余满目黄沙。
循路而去，四周残垣断壁，荒废已久，早无人烟。跋涉良久，行至高处沙丘，见竖井座座，皆已枯竭。
据传，此地曾有一支兵马歇脚，旭日东升之时，马啸声起，兵与马皆望向日升之处，因此得名马头村。如今，名存而人去，恐无人再忆此地耳。
en:
South of Karez, an oasis comes into view, lush and verdant. Wind and sand obstruct the vision of all who approach it. Venturing deeper, heat shimmers, and the oasis vanishes without a trace, leaving nothing but endless yellow sand.
Crumbling walls and ruins greet all who venture further, long abandoned and devoid of human life. Up high over a sand dune, dry vertical shafts dot the horizon.
Legend has it that a military unit once rested here. At sunrise, the horses neighed, and both soldiers and horses gazed toward the east, hence the name Horsehelm Village. Today, the name remains, but the people are gone, and few may remember this place.

zh:
悬泉驿往东，风沙渐息。再向前行，几缕炊烟飘然而升，又有人声吆喝，客商交易，热闹非凡。
村北有一口井渠，据传为旧日掘下之坎儿井，今仍有清水可啜。玉门关苦旱已久，井渠珍贵，故此地得名坎尔孜。
此间村人，皆懂听风，可识风来之处，测风沙起落。曾有人询其秘法，村人眺望悬泉驿，言：
何曾有秘？立于风中守候多年，略懂风之言语耳。
en:
East of Celestial Spring Station, wind and sand gradually subside. Further ahead, wisps of cooking smoke drift upward, mingling with the clamor of voices and the lively trade of merchants.  To the north of the village lies a well canal, said to be a Karez Well dug in ancient times, still yielding clear water for drinking. Jade Gate Pass has suffered from severe drought for ages, making the well extremely precious. Thus, the village was named Karez.
The villagers here all know how to listen to the wind. They can tell where the wind comes from and predict the rise and fall of sandstorms. Once someone asked about their secret technique. The villagers gazed toward Celestial Spring Station and replied, "What secret could there be? We have stood guard in the wind for years and simply learned to understand its language."

zh:
弟子可为师也。

方白曾视一人如父。
但他婉拒了那人的收徒之意，投入文津馆。
他在文津馆中重新习得了自己人生的道路，以玉佩之。
他们都是他的师父。

师者，传道，授业，解惑。
文津馆传他君子之道，授其六艺武功，锻其身，炼其行。
最后于困苦中得出，成为了一枚“玉”。
师曰：万物皆过客，唯心不可折。
en:
A disciple can also be a master.

Fang Bai once viewed a man as his father.
Yet he politely declined the man's offer of apprenticeship and joined the Inkbound Order instead.
In the Inkbound Order, he relearned his path in life, symbolizing it with a jade pendant.
They were all his masters.

A master propagates the doctrine, imparts professional knowledge, and resolves doubts.
The Inkbound Order taught him the way of the gentleman, imparted the Six Arts and martial skills, tempering his body and refining his conduct.
Emerging from hardship, he became a "jade."
The master said: All things are mere travelers; only the will must never break.

楚艳为门阀，秦声是女工。
甲明银得勒，柱触玉玲珑。
猿苦啼嫌月，莺娇语讠尼风。
移愁来手底，送恨入弦中。
赵瑟清相似，胡琴闹不同。
慢弹回断雁，急奏转飞蓬。
霜佩锵还委，冰泉咽复通。
珠联千拍碎，刀截一声终。
倚丽精神定，矜能意态融。
歇时情不断，休去思无穷。
灯下青春夜，樽前白首翁。
且听应得在，老耳未多聋。
en:
[Music I]

[Qin]

Listening to the Monk Jun of Shu Play the Qin
Li Bai
The monk from Shu brings his lute of jade green; down from Mount Emei's peak he comes, serene.
He strums for me a single sweeping tone; as if I hear pines sigh in valleys lone.
My heart is cleansed by flowing stream's refrain; its lingering notes melt into frosty bell's strain.
Unaware, green hills have faded into night; autumn clouds have dimmed the sky's last light.

Listening to Lu Zishun Play the Qin Under the Moon
Li Bai
In the quiet night I sit beneath the moon so bright; the hermit plays his plain qin, a calming sight.
The tune of "Sad Wind" suddenly takes its flight; it echoes like the pines in winter's might.
"White Snow" dances beneath his flying hand; "Green Water" cleanses his heart, a tranquil land.
But Zhong Qi has long gone from this world's strand; no one alive can ever understand.

Listening to Monk Ying's Qin Song
Li He
Clouds leave the shore for Cassia Isle's domain; from Shu's strings come a pair of phoenixes' strain.
Lotus leaves fall, the autumn phoenix flies; the King of Yue by night to Tianmu hies.
Dark pendants worn by pure ministers ring; across the sea, fair brows lead white deer in spring.
Who sees the sword-bearer to Long Bridge stride? Who sees the hair-dipper write on bamboo's side?
The Dharmic monk stands forward at my gate; his brow's high ridge shows truth in solemn state.
The great qin's pegs are eight feet long and straight; old Fengyang wood, not from the tung-tree's fate.
In cool pavilion, strings startle this sick guest; my medicine bag I leave, my rush mat's rest.
Pray sing, but only for the lords and peers; what use is my low office through the years?

Playing the Qin on a Night Boat
Bai Juyi
The birds are perched, the fish lie still and deep; the moon shines on the river in the night so steep.
Outside myself, I have no worldly care; inside the boat, only the qin is there.
The seven strings are friends to me so true; my two ears are the listeners that knew.
When heart is still, the sound grows faint and low; in this I find no ancient or modern, just the flow.

[Zheng]

Listening to the Zheng
Li Duan
The golden-pegged zither sounds so grand; her fair hands play in the jade chamber's strand.
To win the master's lingering glance, with art; she strikes a wrong note now and then, with heart.

Zheng
Bai Juyi
Her cloud-like hair in greenish hues is dressed; her flower face in rosy red is blessed.
Her eyes can cut the autumn water's gleam; her fingers peel the spring onion's green stream.
The Chu's fair style is her noble gate; the Qin's clear tone is her skill innate.
Her silver nails are bright with polished shine; her jade pegs touch with tinkling chime divine.
The ape's sad cry complains the moon's late hour; the oriole's sweet voice speaks to the wind's power.
She draws her grief into her fingertips; she sends her sorrow through the strings and tips.
The Zhao zither's pure notes seem the same; the Hu fiddle's loud stirs a different flame.
A slow tune makes the wild geese seem to part; a quick one whirls the flying reed's art.
Her frost-like pendants tinkle and sway; her icy springs now choke, now flow away.
A thousand beats like pearls break in the air; one single cut ends the tune with a flare.
Her grace refined gives her spirit stead; her pride and skill her moods have wed.
When she stops, her feelings still remain; when she rests, her thoughts retain.
Beneath the lamp, this youth of spring night's time; before the cup, an old man in his prime.
I'll listen, for I ought to hear it all; my aging ears have not yet lost their call.

zh:
兰澳是喜欢念诗的，只觉得朗朗上口，不求甚解。方白是喜欢解诗的，常常不用原句，改来改去地念。
他们那时候都很年轻，喜欢在田埂上散步，在月色下念回环诗。走到夜露深重，方白送她回房，她就坐在灯下，等着熬过这一夜。

诗集在灯下被翻了千百遍，到处都是熟悉的篇章。

冬之夜，夏之日。
百岁之后，归于其室。
方白说，这诗是说相爱的人必定在一起，而你我百岁之后，也定是要同归一处的。
多好的诗。
在蜜恋时，这诗如同蜂糖一样心喜。

夏之日，冬之夜。
百岁之后，归于其居。
多好的诗……
在她放下狠话，头也不回的几千个日夜里，在呻吟和痛苦中，这诗如同黄连一般悲苦。

没有你的日子里夏天煎熬，冬夜是那样漫长难以忍受。
我百岁之后，你会来我的坟头看我吗？我若长眠，会得到一片安宁吗？
无心谷的夜很冷很静。四周仿佛寂寥无人。她忍不住把呜咽藏进了每晚的风里。

葛藤覆盖了一丛丛的黄荆，野葡萄蔓延在荒凉的坟茔。我的爱人长眠在这里，谁与他一起？
葛藤覆盖了一丛丛酸枣枝，野葡萄蔓延在荒凉的坟地。我的爱人埋葬在这里，谁与他在一起？
我生就在这天地间，何处不是痛苦？
他头下的角枕是那样光鲜，他身上的锦被多么光华灿烂。我的爱人安眠在这里，谁与他在一起？
我不能与你在一起，何时不是痛苦？

桃林塞的风很温柔。她的计划和陷阱一样完美。
用惊涛掌的消息做饵，把方白引出。用旧情困住他，用毒针制服他，用剑威逼他。
兰澳把剑收回来的时候，方白倒在了地上。太好了，到此时，她都未尝有一时的犹疑。
但她没有拿到金桃。
方白是不会屈服的，她了解他，就像了解她自己。
他们相爱的日子很短，但这爱恋就像百岁那么长，他们就像同穴共眠那么熟稔。

她没有拿到金桃。金桃，也不能救她。
她要死了。
死是什么？死是冷，是孤独，是痛苦，是再不会有未来的绝望。 
如果这样，那她已经死了一千遍，一万遍了。
死，又有何可怕？
她孤独地留在桃林中。她想起了悍然赴死的方白，想起了屈辱活着的父亲，想起了她被死亡追逐的一生。
群鸟飞过了她。

兰澳告诉小盘，要这样记着她。
我在死亡即将抓住我的时候，先一步转身抱住了它。
我离开这天地，就像飞鸟一样离开了树枝。我并非被狂风卷走，而是挡在了狂风面前。
天地之间如囚笼，我用我的死，打破了这囚笼。

兰澳穿上了文津馆的衣服，易容修饰了自己的身形。她要去作为“方白”赴宴。
即使，在这固若金汤的城池中，这举目皆敌的局面里，这是一个并不高明，成功机会也微乎其微的举措。
愚蠢，好过束手就擒。
没有你的日子里冬夜如此漫长，夏日难耐煎熬。
我将要葬在我的“道”和“义”里。谁与我一起？

众多的刀斧穿过她，最后一瞬间，她好像看到了方白远远赶来。

没有你的日子里夏天煎熬，冬夜漫长孤寒。
我的爱人将葬在他的“道”和“义”里。
谁与他一起？
我与他一起。
en:
Lan Ao cherished the sound of poetry, drawn not to its meaning but to its rhythm and flow. Fang Bai, however, delighted in unraveling its depths, often reshaping verses as he recited them. 
They were young then, wandering along the narrow paths between fields, whispering melodies beneath the moonlight. When the night grew thick with dew, Fang Bai would see her safely home, and she would sit by the lamp, waiting out the long hours until dawn. 

The poetry book lay open before her night after night, its familiar verses etched deep into her heart. 

Winter nights, summer days. 
After death's long journey, return home. 
Fang Bai told her these lines meant that true lovers would find their way back to each other, and that after they died, they would surely be reunited. 
Such a beautiful promise. 
In those days of tender love, the poem was as sweet as honey to her soul. 

Summer days, winter nights. 
After death's long journey, return home. 
How comforting those words seemed... 
But in the endless nights of sorrow and pain that followed, when she finally released those harsh words and refused to look back, the poem turned bitter—like a draught of gall. 

Days without you burned like scorching summers; winters stretched endlessly, cold and unbearable. 
When I am gone, will you come to my grave? If I lie in eternal rest, will peace find me? 
The nights in Hollow Vale were cold and silent; loneliness seemed to envelop all around. She hid her soft weeping in the nightly winds. 

Wisteria wove through thickets of yellow spiny bushes; wild grapes sprawled across the deserted graves. My beloved rests here—who keeps him company? 
Wisteria wove through thickets of sour jujube branches; wild grapes sprawled across the deserted graves. My beloved rests here—who keeps him company? 
I was born into this world—where is pain not found? 
His pillow glows with polish; his embroidered cover gleams with grandeur. My love sleeps here—who shares his rest? 
I cannot be with you—when, then, is my heart not breaking? 

The breeze at Peach Grove Pass was soft, almost tender. Her plan, like the traps she'd woven, was flawless. 
Using the secret of Palm Master Fierceness as bait, she drew Fang Bai out—bound him with memories of their past love, subdued him with poisoned needles, and held him at swordpoint. 
When Lan Ao finally sheathed her blade, Fang Bai lay motionless on the ground. Perfect. Not once had she wavered. 
Yet, she did not claim the Golden Peach. 
Fang Bai would never yield. She knew him as deeply as she knew herself. 
Their love had been brief, yet it stretched across a lifetime—so intimately entwined, as if they shared the same resting place. 

She had failed to seize the Golden Peach, but even that treasure could not save her now. 
She was dying. 
What is death but cold, loneliness, pain—the utter despair of a future forever lost?  
If so, she had already died a thousand times, ten thousand times over. 
What was there left to fear? 
Alone amidst the peach blossoms, she thought of Fang Bai, who faced death without fear; of her father, burdened by shame; and of her own life, relentlessly hunted by death's shadow. 
A flock of birds swept overhead. 

Lan Ao told Xiaopan to remember her thus: 
When death came for me, I turned toward it, enfolding it in my arms. 
I left this world like a bird taking flight from its branch—not swept away by the storm, but standing resolute against it. 
The world is a cage, and with my death, I shattered its bars. 

Dressed in the robes of the Inkbound Order, she altered her appearance by disguise, ready to attend the banquet in Fang Bai's name. 
Even in this fortress, strong as iron and surrounded by foes, where danger lurked in every glance, her chance of success was slim—yet her resolve was unshaken. 
Better to act foolishly than to surrender without a fight. 
Without you, the winters stretch endlessly; the summers burn with unbearable heat. 
I shall be buried with my "Path" and my "Righteousness." Who will stand with me? 

Blades tore through her, and in her final moments, she thought she saw Fang Bai rushing to her side. 

Days without you burned like scorching summers; winters stretched endlessly, cold and unforgiving. 
My beloved will be laid to rest with his "Path" and his "Righteousness." 
Who will stand by him? 
I will.

韩通独坐书房，写着札子，思绪沉浮。先帝晏驾，幼主临朝，汴梁城里的风向愈发晦暗。坊间街巷，明里暗里总有些关于殿前都点检的传闻。韩通其实不愿去深究那些非议，但带兵半辈子磨出来的直觉告诉他，这天太静，静得让人不得不防。

身侧的木箱半敞着，那顶旧兜鍪静静躺在底端。

他那庶子韩守谅回京了。从江南潜回汴梁，在樊楼当起了什么燕乐坊的坊主。身在京城，韩通却一次也没去过樊楼。一来不想暴露儿子暗桩身份，二来，韩家弯弓饮血，进不惯那迎来送往的舞乐之地。

外头总传韩坊主笛琴双绝，乃音律奇才。韩通每次听了只是一声冷哼。只是夜深时，擦甲的手也会顿住。

或许等城里这阵邪风歇了，若是那小子自己懂规矩，全须全尾地滚回家来……或许，可以勉强由着他吹上一曲什么靡靡之音。就一曲。

“将军！急信！”
家仆的惊呼骤来。韩通接过字条，面色一变，如遭雷击。案几被猛地踢翻，将军提起刀便冲了出去——

走得太急，急得他忘了披甲，也忘了脚边半敞的木箱。陪他浴血多年的兜鍪，只好错过了他的最后一战。
en:
Han Tong sat alone in his study, writing a petition as his thoughts drifted. The late Emperor had passed, the young heir had ascended, and the winds in Bianliang were turning dark. In the streets and alleys, rumors about the Palace Guard Commander were spreading. Han Tong didn't want to dwell on the gossip, but his intuition, honed by half a lifetime of leading troops, told him the sky was too quiet: so quiet that one had to be on guard.

The wooden chest beside him was half open, and an old battle helmet lay quietly at the bottom.

His illegitimate son Han Shouliang had returned to the capital. Having sneaked back to Bianliang from Jiangnan, he had become the faction master of Grace Pavilion at Revelry Hall. Despite being in the same city, Han Tong had never visited Revelry Hall. First, he didn't want to expose his son's status as a hidden agent; second, the Han family were archers and warriors, unaccustomed to the entertainment and music of such places.

Rumors said Master Han was a master of both flute and zither, a musical genius. Han Tong would only snort coldly whenever he heard this. But in the deep of night, his hand would pause while polishing his armor.

Perhaps once this ill wind in the city subsided, if the boy knew his place and returned home in one piece... perhaps he would allow him to play some trifling tune. Just one.

"General! An urgent letter!"
The servant's cry came suddenly. Han Tong took the note, and his expression changed as if struck by lightning. He kicked over the table, grabbed his blade, and rushed out...

He left in such a hurry that he forgot to don his armor and forgot the half-open chest by his feet. The battle helmet that had accompanied him through years of bloodshed missed his final battle.

zh: 《诗经》成于周代，乃采自十五国、朝廷郊庙之乐章。全书分风、雅、颂三部，共三百零五篇，以四言为主，兼有杂言，多入韵。所涉祭祀、宴饮、农事、征战、婚恋诸事。西汉立于学官，设博士，为《诗》经学之始。自汉以下，历代推为“温柔敦厚”之教，居儒家六经之首。
en: The Book of Songs was compiled during the Zhou dynasty, gathered from the folk songs of fifteen states and the ceremonial music of the imperial court. The full work is divided into three parts: Airs, Elegant Verses, and Hymns, comprising three hundred and five pieces in total. It was written primarily in four-character verse, with some irregular forms, and largely rhymed. Its subjects encompass ritual offerings, banquets, farming affairs, warfare, and matters of love and marriage. During the Western Han, it was enshrined among the official academies and a designated Scholar was appointed to its study, marking the beginning of the Book of Songs as a classical discipline. From the Han onward, every age has extolled it as a teaching of "gentle and sincere virtue," and it stands first among the Six Classics of Confucianism.

zh: 螺钿紫檀五弦琵琶，镶嵌质地乐器。隋唐时，琵琶东传至朝鲜和日本。据日本史书《三代实录》載，承和二年遣唐使藤原貞敏自唐获赠紫檀琵琶与乐谱。《平家物语》则记有一记传说，有遣唐使承琵琶名手廉承武传授、获赠玄象、青山、狮子丸三面琵琶；归航时，狮子丸因龙神作祟坠海。正仓院琵琶为现存唯一唐五弦琵琶，是唐时期中华文化与海外文化友好交流的见证。
en: The five-string rosewood pipa inlaid with mother-of-pearl is a beautifully crafted instrument. During the Sui and Tang dynasties, it spread to Korea and Japan. According to Japanese records, in the Jōwa era, envoy Fujiwara no Sadatoshi received a pipa and music from Tang China. The Tale of the Heike tells of envoy Ren Shōbu, gifted three pipas, one lost at sea to a sea dragon. The pipa at Shōsōin, the sole surviving Tang-era five-string pipa, symbolizes historic cultural exchange.

zh: 唐开元中，有虎取人家女为妻，于深山结室而居。经二载，其妇不之觉。后忽有二客携酒而至，便于室中群饮，戒其妇云：此客稍异，慎无窥觑。须臾皆醉眠。妇因往视，悉虎也，心大惊骇，而不敢言。久之，虎复为人形，还谓妇曰：得无窥乎？妇言：初不敢离此，后忽云思家，愿一归觐。经十日，夫将酒肉与妇偕行，渐到妻家，遇深水，妇人先渡，虎方褰衣，妇戏云：卿背后何得有虎尾出？虎大惭，遂不渡水，因尔疾驰不返。
en: During the Kaiyuan reign of the Tang Dynasty, a tiger abducted a man's daughter to be his wife and built a house in the deep mountains to live. For two years, the woman did not realize his true identity. Later, two guests suddenly came with wine and drank with him in the house. He warned his wife: "These guests are somewhat unusual; be careful not to peek." Soon, they all fell drunk and asleep. The woman went to look and found that they were all tigers. She was extremely frightened but did not dare to speak. After a long time, the tiger transformed back into a human form and asked his wife: "Did you peek?" The woman replied: "At first, I did not dare to leave here, but later I suddenly missed home and wished to visit my family." After ten days, the husband took wine and meat and traveled with his wife, gradually approaching her home. They encountered deep water; the woman crossed first. As the tiger was lifting his clothes to cross, the woman joked: "Why is there a tiger's tail sticking out from behind you?" The tiger was greatly ashamed, did not cross the water, and galloped away, never to return.

zh:
张豹这一生最大的遗憾，就是寨子的名字没自己的份。

自离开家后，三兄弟叱咤风云，何其威风，聚义落草也得绿林好汉一呼百应。
行走江湖，这寨子也得有个名字。可三人大字都不识几个，起名倒成了燃眉之急。
“啰哩巴嗦，要不叫张家寨！”大哥张龙啧了一声，用野草茎剔了剔牙。
“不好，这名字太烂怂了！”张虎嫌弃地坐下，擦着大刀。
“那……三雄寨？”张豹是三兄弟里最聪明的，自诩比两个哥哥多些见识。
“熊？谁熊？这小子咋灭自己威风！”张虎一拍张豹的后脑勺。”咱们哥仨龙虎豹，个个威风凛凛，怎么就熊了！”
知道哥哥们的斤两，张豹不再说话。“那要不就龙虎豹寨。一人一个字，公平。”
“好是好，但总觉得不顺口。”张虎皱皱眉，看了看张龙。“龙虎豹寨，喊起来麻烦。不如……叫龙虎寨吧！”
张龙点点头。“行，就龙虎寨吧。藏龙卧虎，也霸气，也好记。”
张豹一脸惊讶。“俺还喘气呢！”
“哎呀，老三，你看，离人泪里没眼泪，月亮馍里没月亮，但龙虎寨里是真有豹子！”张虎模仿着市井勾栏的泼皮话，生硬地解释着。
“去去去，这都哪儿跟哪儿！”张豹气得胡子都歪了。“从小你俩就坏！阿爷走以后，你俩成天挤兑俺！要不是有娘在，俺早被你俩饿死了！”

说到张老爹张老娘，三兄弟皆是一愣。张老爹是个屠户——大概是因为这活伤阴德，张老爹早早走了。张老娘一人拉扯三个孩子长大，个中苦楚自不必说。
一碗水终究没法永远端平，这道理张豹也懂得。机灵的他总会利用娘亲来弥补自己吃的亏。——毕竟家里最小的总要更受父母宠爱些。
只是这一次，他实在是太生气了。明明是三兄弟一起打下来的寨子，自己却不能有姓名！

张龙懒得理，直接吩咐手底下去整个大牌匾，把龙虎寨的名字打响。
张虎在一边应和着，全然没管张豹涨得通红的脸。
“直娘贼，老子不跟你俩干了！”踢翻了酒坛，张豹扛着刀走了，只留下张虎一声叹息。

当晚，寨里风清云静。张虎看着窗外的月色，有些担心。
“大哥，俺们这么做，是不是有点过了？”到底还是兄弟，张虎牵挂着老三。
张龙累了，闭着眼养神。“这世道，落草为寇也不是长久之计。万一有一天寨子出了事，咱俩逃不脱，总得让他脱身。”
“豹子脑瓜子灵光，吃不了亏。他认路，想回来就回了。”张龙想了想，补充道：“明天差俩机灵的弟兄去看看他，给他送点酒肉。”
“告诉他，不管寨子叫啥，他永远是三当家。”
en:
Zhang Bao's greatest regret in life was that his name never made it onto the bandit stronghold's sign.

After leaving home, the three brothers had made a fearsome name for themselves. When they gathered to become bandits, even seasoned outlaws answered their call.
A name was essential for their stronghold in the jianghu. But since none of them were well-educated, naming it became a pressing problem.
"Enough dithering! Let's call it Zhang Clan Stronghold!" Eldest brother Zhang Long flicked a weed stem from his teeth.
"Too damn plain!" Zhang Hu wiped his broadsword disdainfully.
"How about... Three Heroes Fort?" Zhang Bao, the cleverest of the trio, ventured.
''Heroes? Who's a 'hero' here? You trying to curse us?'' Zhang Hu smacked Zhang Bao's head. ''We're named for the Long, tiger, and leopard—all fierce as hell. Why call it heroes?"
Knowing his brothers' limits, Zhang Bao swallowed his pride. "How about 'Claw & Spot Fort'? For the claws of the Long and tiger, and the spots of my namesake, the leopard?"
"Sounds clunky," Zhang Hu muttered, eyeing Zhang Long. "Tiger Fort—that's snappier!"
Zhang Long nodded. "Done. 'Tiger Fort'. Imposing. Memorable."
Zhang Bao's jaw dropped. "I'm still breathing here!"
"Ah, little brother! 'Parting Tears' has no tears, 'mooncake' has no moon, but by golly, Tiger Fort has a real leopard!" Zhang Hu tried to imitate patter of market square snake oil salesman with his forced explanation.
''Ugh, what nonsense is that!?'' Zhang Bao's beard twitched with anger. ''You two have been bullying me since we were kids! After Grandpa died, you'd have starved me to death if not for Mother!''

At the mention of their parents, the brothers fell silent. Their father, a butcher, had died young, probably from the ill karma of his trade. Their mother had raised all three alone, enduring untold hardships.
Zhang Bao knew life wasn't always fair. As the youngest, he'd always used their mother's favor to even the odds. After all, the baby of the family gets spoiled.
But this time, he was livid. They'd built the fort together, yet his name was being erased!

Zhang Long ignored him, ordering men to carve a huge signboard and spread the name Tiger Fort far and wide.
Zhang Hu agreed, oblivious to Zhang Bao's red-faced rage.
"Screw you both! I'm done with you two!" Zhang Bao kicked over a wine jar and stormed out, blade on his shoulder. Zhang Hu sighed.

That night, the fort was calm under clear skies. Zhang Hu stared at the moon, worried.
''Did we go too far?'' He still cared for his youngest brother.
Zhang Long, eyes closed, was tired. ''In this world, being bandits isn't a lifelong gig. If the fort ever falls, we might have to go down with it, but he shouldn't have to.''
''Bao's smart. He won't suffer, and he knows the way back.'' Zhang Long added after a pause: ''Send two sharp men tomorrow to check on him and bring him wine and meat.''
''Tell him no matter the fort's name, he'll always be our third chief.''

Jadecho Bay lies on the northern side of Goldentone Ridge. The ridge drops steeply away, opening suddenly onto the sea. At high tide, waves wash over the rocks with a sound like shattered jade, giving the bay its name and echoing Goldentone Ridge in beginning and end. Across a narrow inlet, a reef rises from the sea. 《辽史·食货志》有云：“契丹旧俗，其富以马，其强以兵。纵马於野，弛兵於民。有事而战，彍骑介夫，卯命辰集。马逐水草，人仰湩酪，挽强射生，以给日用，糗粮刍茭，道在是矣。以是制胜，所向无前。”契丹为游牧民族，素有逐水草而牧马之习俗，自辽国建立，六院之下专设马群司，掌彰愍宫马群牧养蕃息之事。契丹战马素以耐劳善忍、勇猛稳健著称，故名“契丹铁蹄”。
契丹铁蹄体格较小，肢粗而短，蹄小而圆，蹄质坚实，不易裂缝，步伐敏捷，即便于崎岖山路亦如履平地。性沉稳，耐粗饲，易增膘，寿命长，可负重乘骑，为契丹辽国最常见的马种。
en:
The Jade Book states, "Fierce and brave." Biao describes a swift-moving horse with small spots scattered through its coat. Khitan Iron Hooves bearing this pattern are called Wubiao.
The History of Liao records, "In old Khitan custom, wealth lay in horses, and strength in arms. Horses roamed the wilds; soldiers worked in the mass. When war arose, armored riders and soldiers gathered at dawn by royal command. Horses were raised by nature; people relied on dairy. They hunted live prey to meet daily needs. Travel, supplies, and fodder all followed this way and were drawn from local resources. Victory came from it, unstoppable in battle." As nomads, the Khitan raise horses along rivers and pastures. With the founding of the Liao Dynasty, they established a dedicated Horse Herd Office under the Six Bureaus to manage the imperial herds of Zhangmin Palace. Khitan warhorses are famed for endurance, strength, and composure, earning the title "Khitan Iron Hooves."
Khitan Iron Hooves are compact in build, with short, sturdy limbs and small, round hooves that rarely crack. Nimble-footed, they move easily even across rugged terrain. Calm in nature, tolerant of rough feed, quick to gain weight, long-lived, and capable of carrying both riders and loads, they are the most common horse in the Liao dynasty.

zh:
王清、王清。
在贺然十岁时，听见身边的人叫将军名字时，他就在心里一遍一遍地复述这个名字，但他永远会谨慎又尊崇地给这个名字后再冠上那个身份——王清将军，王清将军。
可他是什么样的人，是被世上剩下的人，无家、无父无母、无处可去，世上最微不足道的人，以至于看什么都显得很高大，何况王清本就是高高在上的将军，是世间唯一捡起他的人，是他这辈子想要仰望的人。
以至于，多年之后，他努力走到王清身边的那刻，他以为自己的赤忱藏得很好，他努力压抑着自己心绪的起伏，他将雀跃的尾音用力道抚平，他将仰慕的神态收敛在垂眸的瞬间。
但如果有些名姓在已在唇齿间翻涌多年，一身皮肉如何能压过嵌入半生的执念。
特别是——
王清将军说：“我记得你。“
记得。
人是不会妄想距离自己太远的东西。
他只是窥探那遥远事物落下的地方，他嫉妒了很多年王清对于江晏的照顾，他窥视着王清看向江晏的神态，他一直、一直以为他想要得到的是同样的赏识和垂怜，可在那一刻，他却发现。
他和江晏不一样，原来小到将军的一点记得，就足以填满他想要的一切。
他几乎要脱口而出，他来到这里经历了什么，他马上就可以投入他的麾下了。
别急，再等一会，再等一会，他还会再见到他。
他和将军会有下一面，再下一面。
将军会不止是记得他。
他扬起脸，露出一个十年前一般青涩的笑。
en:
Wang Qing. Wang Qing.
When He Ran was ten, he'd hear people call the general's name, and he'd quietly repeat it to himself, over and over. But he would always add the title, with respect and awe, General Wang Qing, General Wang Qing.
But who was he, really? Just one of the world's forgotten, with no home, no parents, nowhere to go. He was so insignificant that everything seemed out of reach, towering above him. And Wang Qing was towering in every way, an untouchable general, the only person in the world who ever noticed him, the one person he longed to look up to all his life.
So even years later, when he finally worked his way close to Wang Qing, he thought he'd hidden his feelings well. He tried to steady his voice, to smooth out any excitement, and to mask his admiration by keeping his gaze low.
But if you've whispered a name to yourself for years, how could mere flesh and bone hide an obsession that's carved itself into your life?
Especially when—General Wang Qing said, "I remember you."
He remembered.
People don't dare to hope for things that feel too far away.
All He Ran ever did was watch from a distance, jealous for years of how much attention Wang Qing gave Jiang Yan. He'd study every look Wang Qing gave Jiang Yan, thinking all he wanted was that same approval, that same kindness. But in that moment, he realized that...
He wasn't like Jiang Yan at all. For him, just being remembered was enough to fill every empty space inside.
He almost blurted out everything he'd gone through to get here, how close he was to finally serving under Wang Qing's command.
Wait a little longer, he told himself. Just a little longer.
There would be another meeting, and another after that.
It wouldn't end with just being remembered.
He lifted his face, unable to hide the shy, youthful smile he'd worn so many years ago.

zh:
那一夜，凉州降下了三天三夜的暴雪。
清玉岸的泉水结冰，无垢塔的钟声黯哑。就连能翻越祁连山的骆驼也熬不住极寒，冻毙在了玉露台的路边。

有人看到，公主手持琉璃烛盏，素衣淡妆，步步走入望帝乡，再无回头。
冰霜吞没了整座望帝乡，公主终究没能回到她日思夜想的长安。
别鹤居外，宫娥亦着缟素，牵手走向了结冰的玉池深处。

大雪肆虐了三天，望帝乡被玄冰覆盖。三日后，百姓牵挂公主安危，聚于玉露台悬樽山高声呼喊公主。只见明月掩映，望帝乡如同琉璃棺椁岿然不动。风吹之时，塔身孔窍竟发出呜咽之声。
众人悲戚，尝以利刃破冰而入。然望帝乡中再无公主身影，唯有一支素雅的步摇。

人们感念公主恩泽，将望帝乡视为离月光最近的地方。有酿酒师尝试攀登高塔，最后将自己的酒也留在了这里。
又有父老感念那宫娥殉主的气节，在玉池别鹤居立像作为纪念。
en:
On that night, a heavy snowstorm fell on Liangzhou, lasting three days and three nights. 
The spring water at Clear Jade Shore froze solid, and the bell of Purity Pagoda grew hoarse. Even the camels that could cross the Qilian Mountains couldn't withstand the extreme cold, freezing to death by the roadside of Jade Dew Terrace. 

Someone saw the princess holding a glazed candle holder, dressed in plain white with light makeup, walking step by step into imperial capital, never to look back. 
Frost and ice engulfed the entire imperial capital. In the end, the princess never returned to Chang'an, the city she missed day and night. 
Outside the Crane Retreat, the palace maids also dressed in white mourning clothes, holding hands and walking into the depths of the frozen Jade Pond. 

The heavy snow raged for three days, covering imperial capital in black ice. Three days later, concerned about the princess's safety, the people gathered at Chalice Peak by Jade Dew Terrace and called out to her loudly. Under the moonlight, imperial capital stood still like a glazed coffin. When the wind blew, the holes in the pagoda tower let out a whimpering sound. 
Grieving, the crowd tried to break the ice with sharp blades and enter. But there was no sign of the princess in imperial capital, only an elegant hairpin. 

Grateful for the princess's kindness, people regarded imperial capitak as the place closest to the moonlight. A winemaker tried to climb the tall tower and finally left his wine here. 
The elders, moved by the palace maids' loyalty to their mistress, erected a statue at the Crane Retreat by the Jade Pond in their memory.

zh:

后来沙暴来了，也疏浚过坎尔孜的井。
再后来，又来到了这里。
他知道，脚下的这口井只是将军水系图中并不起眼的一个点。
但就是这样的点，一个与一个相连，
连通了这里与坎尔孜，又连通了整个河西。
最终还会流到大唐去。
脚下的泥土洇出了水，周围的人开始起哄，
让他抓紧投个填井之物，讨个好寓意。
他解下几枚大唐的钱，钱的中间宛似一口“井眼”。
他用红绳把铜钱绑成了一个佩的样子，
将所有井眼连在了一起。
en:
Yuan Xi had dug many wells. The first were at Jade Gate Pass. 
Later, when sandstorms came, he dredged wells at Karez. 
Then he came here. 
He knew the well beneath his feet was just an unremarkable point on the general's water map. 
But it was points like these, connected one to another, 
that linked this place to Karez, and Karez to all of Hexi— 
and would one day flow all the way to the Tang. 
Water seeped into the soil underfoot. The crowd urged him to
 throw in a closing offering for good luck. 
He took out several Tang coins—their square holes like tiny "well-eyes." 
Threading them with red cord into an amulet, 
he linked every well-eye together.
About time!

zh:
瞌睡的本事是在哪都能睡，因而得了此名。露台上打得震天响，它睡。车赛发令号角吹得人耳朵疼，它睡。食堂开饭，大伙儿端着碗从它身边跑过，它翻个身，继续睡。有热心行人忧心它是不是聋了，凑过去在它耳边咪咪喵喵的唤，它睁开一只眼，看了那人一下，又闭上了。
没聋，就是懒得理你。
但有一个时候它不睡。每天傍晚，太阳快落山的时候，它会爬起来，走到历城台最高的地方，面朝西边，安安静静地坐着，看日落。谁也不知道一只猫看日落能看出什么名堂。但那个时辰，如果有人从墙下经过，抬头看见一团胖橘蹲在墙头，被夕阳镀上一层金边，会觉得这一天好像也没那么糟。
en:
Sleepyhead's greatest skill is the ability to sleep anywhere, which is exactly how it got its name. When thunderous sparring shakes the terrace, it sleeps. When the racing horns blow loud enough to hurt people's ears, it sleeps. When it is mealtime at the dining hall and everyone runs past it carrying bowls, it simply rolls over and continues to sleep.

Some well-meaning passersby worry if it might be deaf. They lean in close and make "pspsps" noises or meow into its ear. It opens one eye, gives the person a glance, and closes it again.

It is not deaf; it just cannot be bothered to pay attention to you.

But there is one time when it does not sleep. Every evening, just as the sun is about to set, it gets up, walks to the highest point of Licheng Terrace, faces west, and sits quietly to watch the sunset. No one knows what profound meaning a cat could possibly find in a sunset. But at that hour, if someone passes beneath the wall and looks up to see a cat squatting on the edge, rimmed in gold by the setting sun, they might feel that their day was not so bad after all.
It actually gave me something good!

zh:
《玉京归梦》

一曲惊舟湖上，不知归梦难留。玉京多情故人，弦上话说从头。

像江逸这样弱冠年纪便精通百般乐器的人，照理是可以狂妄的。但他其实没这个心情。于他来说，音乐只是语言的一种。字句说不清的东西，用音律偏能顺畅地说出来，于是江逸自然而然地终日与乐为伍，回过神来才听说自己被人称道“音律奇才”。但这门语言就像一种偏门的家乡话，知者甚少。大多数时，江逸只是一个漂泊的失乡之人。
所以当醉花阴邀他入樊楼奏乐赏曲，江逸是很高兴的。他知醉花阴有燕乐坊精研音律，有好乐亦有好乐人，于是急匆匆就赶去。

那是一个很好的日子。前往樊楼的花船上，江逸都已坐不住，立在船头，一靠岸便跳了上去。引荐者带他至燕乐坊，还未见人，先闻笛声。
耳朵一亮，心却一沉。那笛声清越，技巧无可挑剔，音色是明亮的，可亮色其下却是一股郁结。江逸不知乐手是谁，经历如何，但他为这笛声难过。
他在那人身后站定。在一首曲子的光景里，江逸就只是安静地看他。此人身材瘦削，笛声却气息充盈，声有贯天地之势。而当他转身看到江逸时，自然是吓了一跳，问他是谁。

“我是江逸，受邀来樊楼演乐”——原本只要这样说便好了，但他忽然激动得说不出话。那隐约好似将要靠岸的激动。他三步并作两步，坐到一旁的琴边，抚了一首曲子。乐音流出，方才所闻笛声中的叹息化入指间。一曲终了，他才抬起头。之前的吹笛人已坐在琴前，问他：“这曲子有名字吗？”
江逸这才开口：“只是随兴而弹。”
“有归人之细微情意，又有山海之大气；有‘海上明月共潮生’的妙丽，又有‘人生代代无穷已’的洒脱。叫《山海归梦》如何？”
江逸想想，点点头：“名字很好。”
那人冷不丁地又说：“你是江逸。”
“是我。先生是？”
他却没回答，只是一笑：“我为你的曲子取了个名字，那你给我的也取一个？”
“我不擅长取名，也不擅长说话，这才以琴代言。”
“原来如此。你说得很好。”吹笛人点了点他放在弦上的手。
“师傅怎在调笑贵客！”一个轻巧的女声打断他们。一位略显稚嫩的女子走进屋子，“江先生，您一转眼就不见了，原来您已经自己来见坊主了。”
江逸恍然：“坊主……这位是燕乐坊坊主，难怪笛声如此动人。”
坊主道：“与江先生或可相提并论？”
江逸连忙拱手：“远不比坊主先生。”
“坊主先生叫着生分，叫我韩微就好。玉茗，江先生的住处可安排好了？”
“都安排妥当。”唤作凌玉茗的娘子眉毛一挑，“方才我在楼下听有人抚琴，大气潇洒，不似师傅平日的琴声。原来是江逸先生弹的？真好听。”
韩微道：“什么意思，说我弹琴小气？”
凌玉茗嬉笑：“不及江先生气度！”
江逸红着脸打断：“你们夸得也太过头了，我无非就会得乐器多一些……韩先生年纪轻轻已是坊主，造诣自然比我高得多。”
凌玉茗叹气：“你听听，‘无非会得多一些’！听你们这些天才说话真是气死庸人。”
江逸瞪大眼睛，连连摆手：“我我我……我没这个意思，姑娘你……你的手指很长，很适合弹琴，怎会是庸人！”
韩微拍手大笑：“江先生百般乐器精通，这张嘴却是实在不太好使！”
江逸被人笑话却也没恼，收了笑，轻声道：“还是先生的笛声厉害，把话都说尽了。”
于是韩微就此一怔。
幽幽花香穿过厅堂。江逸到访之前，京城刚下过一场大雨，此时雨过天晴，高楼风好，琴曲余音荡漾；此时艳湖十曲的约定还没立下，韩微尚未遗世，江逸不曾归隐，凌玉茗还不是那个忧愁的花信风。那些举世无双的曲子还只是无名的随兴之作。而终将扑面的死亡与遗憾也只潜伏暗处，尚未露出爪牙。
那真是一个很好的日子。
en:
Dreams Returning to the Capital 

The zither's music spreads across the lake in gentle waves, a quiet sigh for how fate—not we—decides our meetings and farewells. In the capital, old bonds run deep, and through each lingering note, the stories of the past are softly told anew. 

Jiang Yi, though barely twenty, is already a virtuoso on countless instruments. By all rights, he could be arrogant—but he's not. To him, music is simply another language. What words cannot fully express, melodies carry with graceful ease. So naturally, he spends his days immersed in music, only gradually realizing others regard him as a "musical prodigy." Yet this language he speaks is rare, a dialect known to few, and most days, Jiang Yi feels like a wanderer far from home. 
That's why, when Velvet Shade invited him to perform at Revelry Hall and enjoy a night of music, Jiang was genuinely delighted. He knew Velvet Shade was closely connected with Grace Pavilion—a place famed for its masterful musicians and exquisite instruments—and so he hurried over without a moment's delay. 

It was a perfect day. On the flower-laden boat approaching Revelry Hall, Jiang could hardly contain himself; he stood at the bow, and the moment they reached shore, he leapt off the boat. Guided inside Grace Pavilion, he hadn't even caught sight of anyone before the sound of a flute reached his ears. 
His senses sharpened, yet a weight settled in his chest. The flute's tone was crystal clear, the technique flawless, and its timbre brilliantly radiant. But beneath that shining clarity lingered a profound sorrow, a hidden ache. Jiang didn't know who the player was or what trials he had endured, but the sadness in that music touched him deeply. 
He stood quietly behind the flutist, watching in silence as the melody unfolded. The man was slender, yet the breath behind his flute filled the room with a power that seemed to pierce through the skies. When the flutist finally turned and caught sight of Jiang, he startled, asking softly who the newcomer was. 

He had meant only to say, "I'm Jiang Yi, invited to perform at Revelry Hall," but the words caught in his throat, swept away by a sudden surge of emotion—like the quiet thrill of a boat drawing close to shore. Instead, he rushed to a nearby zither and let his hands speak for him. As the melody unfurled, the quiet ache he had heard in that flute earlier wove itself naturally into his playing. When the final note faded, he finally raised his head. The flutist was already seated opposite him at the zither bench, asking, "Does this piece have a name?" 
Jiang found his voice. "I just played what came to me." 
"There's the delicate longing of someone returning home, the vast breath of mountains and seas; a touch of the beauty in the moonlit sea, and the freedom of life flowing on through countless generations. What do you think of calling it ‘Dream of Mountains and Seas'?" 
Jiang considered it and then nodded. "It's a beautiful name." 
The man suddenly added, "So, you are Jiang Yi." 
"I am. And you, sir?" 
He didn't answer. He only smiled. "I named your piece. Shouldn't you name mine?" 
"I'm not good at naming things. I'm not good with words at all. That's why I let the music speak." 
"Ah. And you speak it well." The flutist tapped lightly on the hand Jiang still rested on the strings. 
"Master, how can you tease an honored guest like that!" A lively young voice cut in. A girl, still with a touch of youthful innocence, stepped into the room. "Master Jiang, you disappeared in an instant—I see you found the pavilion master all on your own." 
Jiang suddenly realized, "So this is the master of Grace Pavilion—no wonder the flute sounded so captivating." 
The master smiled, "Do you think you're on equal footing with me, Master Jiang?" 
Jiang quickly cupped his hands respectfully, "Far from it, Master Han." 
"Please, no need for such formalities—just call me Han Wei. Yuming, has Master Jiang's lodging been arranged?" 
"All taken care of," replied Ling Yuming, raising an intrigued brow. "Earlier, I caught the sound of a zither downstairs—bold and free, quite unlike your usual style. So it was Master Jiang? Truly exquisite." 
Han chuckled, "Are you implying my playing is stingy?" 
Ling teased gently, "Not nearly as grand as Master Jiang's." 
Blushing, Jiang hurried to interrupt, "You flatter me too much. I simply happen to know more instruments... As the young master of Grace Pavilion, Master Han outperforms me by far." 
Ling sighed with a smile, "Listen to that—‘just happen to know more instruments.' Hearing geniuses speak so modestly can frustrate the rest of us." 
Jiang's eyes widened as he waved his hands nervously, "No, no, not at all! Miss, your fingers are long and graceful—perfect for playing. You could never be ordinary!" 
Han laughed heartily, "Master Jiang may master many instruments, but he sure is shy of his words!" 
Taking their teasing in stride, Jian smiled softly, "Still, it's your flute, Master Han, that truly speaks—the words music cannot express." 
Han fell silent, a thoughtful look crossing his face. 
A delicate floral fragrance drifted through the hall. Before Jiang's arrival, rain had swept through the capital. Now, under clear skies and a gentle breeze weaving between the tall buildings, the lingering echoes of music filled the air. At this moment, the promise of the legendary "Ten Ballads of Pearlglow Lake" had yet to be made; Han was not yet withdrawn from the world; Jiang had not yet retreated into seclusion; and Ling was far from the wistful Flower Messenger she would become. Those unmatched melodies were still nameless, spontaneous creations, and the shadows of inevitable loss and sorrow lay quietly in wait, claws yet concealed. 
It was, in truth, a perfect day.

现在，命运的齿轮开始转动，距离将我救出宝箱只差最后一步，那就是往宝箱中掷入一丢丢铜钱，以示恩义！因这箱子被丢在九流门驻地，过路人只以为这是个骗局，卡在了这最后一步，真是糊涂！
但我看得出来，您和他们不一样！您一定就是我命定的主人！钱儿叮当一响，箱神闪亮登场，我将立马实现您的所有愿望！
en:
At last, you're here—the one I've been waiting for all this time, my destined savior. I am the spirit bound to this treasure chest!  

When I was sealed inside this chest, I silently vowed: Whoever frees me from this chest, I will grant their every wish! 

Now, the wheel of fate has turned, and you're just one step away from setting me free: simply drop a few coins into the chest as a sign of goodwill!

But since this chest was left at the Nine Mortal Ways Base, passersby thought it was a trick and never took that final step—such a shame! 

But I can tell—you're different. You are the master Destiny has chosen for me! Let the coins ring out, and I'll appear in a flash to make all your wishes come true.

First Letter:
I've been all alone for over three days. Tell me, my lady—when will you come back?

Second Letter:
I hope you can understand that ruling a nation and securing peace demands swift, resolute action. The Cup of Wine Policy remains the most effective method to maintain order. I bear no guilt, yet Zheng Yi betrayed the Zhao family for Shadow Arsenal, threatening my life. How could I possibly forgive such treachery?

Third Letter:
After deep reflection and sorrow, I finally feel the weight of your concerns. You come from the jianghu, where loyalty and honor reign supreme, and naturally could not abide by my ways. I spared Zheng Yi's life then, and from now on I shall tread more carefully... My lady, when shall you return?

zh: “取清酒，澄三五日后，据酒多少取瓮一口，先净刷洗讫，以火烘干。于底旁钻一窍子如筋粗，以柳屑子塞定，将酒入在瓮，入黄蜡半斤，瓮口以油单纸盖系定...于当门里着炭三秤笼令实，于中心着半斤许，熟火便用闭门，门外更悬席帘，七日后方开，又七日方取吃。取时以细竹子一茶头边夹少许新棉，款款抽塞子，以器承之；以绢竹子遍于瓮搅缠尽着底。浊物清，即休缠，仍塞了(先钻窍子，图取淀浊易耳)。每取时却入一竹筒子，如钢淋子，旋取之，即耐停不损，全胜于煮酒也。”
en: "Take clear wine and let it settle for 3–5 days. Prepare a clean jar, scrubbed and fire-dried. Drill a small hole (chopstick-width) at the base, plugged with willow shavings. Pour in the wine, add 250g of yellow wax, and seal the jar mouth with oiled paper. Place 3L of tightly packed charcoal inside, ignite a small fire (half a jin of charcoal) at the center, then shut the door and hang a reed curtain outside. After 7 days, open it; after another 7 days, the wine is ready. To serve, insert a thin bamboo tube tipped with cotton, gently remove the plug, and drain into a vessel. Stir thoroughly with a silk-wrapped bamboo stick until the sediment settles and the wine clears. Reseal the hole (pre-drilled for easier sediment removal). For serving, always use a filtered bamboo tube to draw the wine gradually. This keeps it stable and unspoiled, far superior to boiled wine."

zh: 破阵乐源自唐初的秦王破阵之曲，最初为军歌，后演变为唐朝的宫廷乐舞，用于宴享、祭祀等场合，气势磅礴、震天动地。唐高宗时的《神功破阵乐》、唐玄宗时的《小破阵乐》皆为唐太宗所订《秦王破阵乐》的形式流变，可惜国内已无遗存，幸有日本唐传古谱多种传世，得以让后人一窥唐乐之貌。然古谱解译殊为困难，复原之路任重道远，今以十六声抛砖引玉，愿与诸君共勉！
en: The piece originated from the early Tang Dynasty's Qin King's Battle Music, which was first composed as a military anthem and later evolved into a form of imperial court musical dance performed during banquets and rituals. Grand and thunderous in tone, it embodied martial valor and ceremonial majesty. During Emperor Gaozong of Tang's reign, the Divine Power Battle Music, and under Emperor Xuanzong of Tang, Lesser Battle Music, were both derived from Prince of Qin's Triumph, originally commissioned by Emperor Taizong of Tang. Though this version has vanished within China, others survived in ancient Japanese transcriptions, offering a rare glimpse into the splendor of Tang court music. Yet deciphering these old scores proves extremely challenging, and efforts to reconstruct the original pieces remain arduous. Today, this modest rendition of sixteen tones is offered as a humble start. May it inspire all who share this passion to continue the work.

小禄想，大侠是不是去江湖了？江湖好玩吗？江湖在哪里呀？
小褔大喊：“那我们就去问问嘛！”
三人跑进鬼市子，问牛头，牛头说，江湖嘛，就是刀啊剑啊的一通乱打。
小禄摇摇头，这真没意思。
她们问银婆婆，银婆婆说，这里就是啊。
小寿摇摇头，这里？鬼市子算是江湖吗？
道主们到茶馆里听说书。鬼先生又在讲与契丹的大战，讲朱帮主，讲鬼市子的阴兵。
道主们点点头，哦，对了，这我们知道的，这真是江湖呢！可是先生，江湖人不是都来来去去找不见的，阴兵怎么一直在这里？
鬼先生道：“大抵是心愿未偿。”
“什么心愿？”
先生道：“或是未曾得见——
#Y【鼠鼠生威】——鼠鼠生威，门下弟子不受欺凌。#E”
en:
As night fell, the lanterns of the Ghostlight Market rose again, as they had through countless turnings of day and night. Yet the wanderer who once recklessly stumbled into this place has not returned for a long, long time.
Lu wondered if the hero had gone off into the jianghu. Was the jianghu a fun place? And where exactly was it?
"Then let's go ask!" Fu cried out.
The three ran into the Ghostlight Market and asked Niu Tou. Niu Tou replied, "The jianghu? It's just a chaotic brawl of clashing sabers and swords."
Lu shook her head. That didn't sound like any fun at all.
Then they asked Granny Yin. Granny Yin said, "Why, this place right here is the jianghu."
Shou shook her head. "Here? Does the Ghostlight Market count as the jianghu?"
The Dao Lords went to the teahouse to listen to storytelling. Mr. Ghost was there again, telling of the great war with the Khitan, of Chief Zhu, and of the spectral soldiers of the Ghostlight Market.
The Dao Lords nodded. "Oh, right, we know that part. This really is the jianghu! But sir, aren't people of the jianghu always coming and going without a trace? Why have the spectral soldiers stayed here all this time?"
Mr. Ghost said, "Most likely, their final wishes remain unfulfilled."
"What wishes?"
Mr. Ghost replied, "Perhaps they never lived to see...

"Human birth is rare, and even rarer is life in the central land. Even if one is born, it is difficult to encounter the true teaching. Many stray from the Dao and fall into heresy. 传云，神鸟曷为隐去？一曰，神鸟既知天命，不欲再扰俗世。又或曰，神鸟遁入九天，人间踪影难觅。
今旋行至此，所视岩上草木葱翠，雀吟声声，皆非昔日神鸟之鸣。四周岩壁险峻，崖渊峭拔。山有行道，不及足半。此非常人能涉也。

en:
Legend has it that on the western slopes of Hidden Mountain, there lived a divine bird. Its song rang like temple chimes, clear as nature's own symphony. Thus, the elders named this place Spiritroost Crag. But its song has faded over time and can no longer be heard.
Some say the bird vanished after learning heavenly secrets; others believe it flew beyond Heaven, never to return.
Here, the cliffs are steep, paths are too narrow for a footstep, and only ordinary birds chirp among the thick trees.
Travelers, beware. Don't let curiosity lead you into danger.

zh:
世有更迭，城有迁移。不见山西隅，曾有一墨城旧址，为墨门故地。昔年墨者聚此，研技论道，薪火鼎盛。后地动突起，垣墉倾圮，坊巷湮沉，旧城遂废。仅余学舍，不复有人居。唯城隅占风铎存焉，悬残谯之檐，历千载而不坠。逢风吹铎响，多有异象，人言其存古来之声。 
今临故地，蹑荒榛，抚断碣，闻旧城声，见旧城事。或可借铎响之机，一窥千年墨门故事。
en:
The world changes, and cities rise and fall. On the western edge of Hidden Mountain lies the Old Mohist City, once the vibrant heart of the Mohists. Here they gathered to study, create, and exchange ideas, their legacy flourishing for generations.
Then a sudden upheaval shattered the city, leaving only the abandoned study, empty and silent. At the corner of the ruins the wind chimes still hang, and when the wind sets them ringing, strange signs are said to appear, carrying echoes of the old city.
Now, wandering these forgotten grounds, one can almost hear the murmurs of the past and glimpse the stories lost to time. Witness the ancient legacy of the Mohists through the wind chime's haunting toll.

For each comprehension objective achieved in the path trial, you can obtain 10 Uncut Jades and earn one star on the star reward screen, which can be obtained repeatedly when the path trial is reset.
On the star reward screen, when earned stars reach the specified level, you can claim a corresponding star reward. Star rewards from Normal and True Ascension chapters are #Ycalculated separately#E. When the path trial is reset, this part of the reward will be reset.
Uncut Jade can be used to exchange for rewards in the Path Trial Shop. There is an upper limit of the obtainable Uncut Jade in each path trial challenge period, with a maximum of 600 obtainable.
Complete all comprehension objectives in any path trial chapter to obtain a time-limited badge and title. Complete all comprehension objectives in any True Ascension chapter to obtain a display badge. When the path trial is reset, you need to challenge again to obtain them.

zh:
行至绿洲旁的村庄，少年听到了人们饥饿的哭声。
他蹲下，握着孤童瘦骨嶙峋的手。饥饿的目光几乎灼伤了他。
“看到这个网了么？它可以把月光变成白面馍馍。”
在众人好奇的目光中，他第一次在外人面前掏出了捞月网。
“月亮光光，快把网张！吃个馍馍，娃娃骑骆驼——”唱起儿时父母哄自己的歌谣，他将手中的捞月网丢向绿洲浅浅的水塘。回到手中的，便是一块足以救命的馍馍。
他将馍馍递给了孤童。身后的人群一阵惊呼。
”敢问仙人何名？“白发苍苍的老者拭着浑浊的眼泪，向着少年虔诚询问。
那一刻少年想到了家乡的传说——月御望舒，可驾车行于九天，洒月华于乾坤。
”我名……”少年抬手指了指月亮，“望舒郎。”
en:
Arriving at a village beside an oasis, the young man heard the cries of hungry people.
He crouched down, holding the bony hand of an orphan. The gaze of hunger nearly scorched him.
"See this net? It can turn moonlight into soft white buns."
Under the curious eyes of the crowd, he drew out his moon-catching net for the first time before outsiders.
"Moonlight bright, cast your net right! Eat a bun, little one rides a camel—" Singing the rhyme his parents had hummed to him in childhood, he tossed the net into the oasis's shallow pond. What returned to his hand was a bun substantial enough to save a life.
He handed the bun to the orphan. A gasp of awe rose from the crowd behind him.
"May I ask your name, Immortal?" An elderly man with white hair wiped away his tears, his eyes clouded, addressing the youth with reverence.
In that moment, the youth thought of the legend from his homeland—Wangshu, the moon's charioteer, who drove across the nine heavens, scattering moonlight upon the world.
"My name is..." The youth raised a hand, pointing at the moon. "...Wangshu."

zh:
长安大寒，雪盈六尺。
盲人乐师兄妹点雪、听梅操琴笛于灞桥古梅下，梨园弟子蓝何行经驻听，遂取洞箫相和。虽不交一言，宫商互应，如契心曲。
三人树下饮酒论乐，不觉已至夜深。蓝何酡然道：习箫三载，技臻至境，然常困于一音，斟酌竟日——洞箫因风成曲，可这风却是天地间最不可捉摸之物，何以御之？

笛师听梅闻之，遂解下腰间布囊相赠，道：我自幼目盲，敏于风息，可“视”其流。因不知如何向他人描述，故以此法显之——取蒹葭内膜，烧制成灰，置于箫笛空洞之中，便可明察风气之流转。

蓝何试之，但见灰随音舞：初引宫调，葭灰如缕；次发商音，灰散若尘；及转角徵，灰涌似泉，杂糅千声。 
曲终灰歇，蓝何叹曰：习箫千日，今始悟道——人籁合天地之律，存焉。

三人竟夜论乐，共谱《岁寒三友》，松竹二阕，音成天然，唯梅花一阕，不得其髓。三人相约，来日再聚，再谱梅曲。
曙色将明，雪霁别去，遗音在树。
en:
In the great cold of Chang'an, snow piled six feet high. 
The blind musician siblings, Seren Snow and Plum Melody, played the guqin and flute under the ancient plum tree at Ba Bridge. When passing by, Masked Troupe Disciple Lan He stopped to listen and then took out his bamboo flute to join in harmony. Without exchanging a single word, their notes resonated, as if sharing a heartfelt melody. 
The three drank and discussed music under the tree until it was deep into the night. Lan He, flushed with wine, said, "Though perfectly skilled after learning the bamboo flute for three years, I remain puzzled by one thing. The bamboo flute creates melodies with the wind, but the wind is the most elusive force in the world. How can one control it?" 

Hearing this, the flutist Plum Melody gave a cloth pouch to Lan He, saying, "Blind since childhood, I am sensitive to the wind's movements, able to 'see' its flow. Knowing not how to describe it to others, I visualize it this way—burn the inner membrane of reeds to ash and place it inside the hollow of the flute to clearly show the flow." 

Lan He tried it and saw the ash dance with the music: when he played the Gong note, the ash flowed like threads to the gong note, scattered like dust to the Shang note, and surged like a spring, blending with a thousand sounds to the Jue and Zhi notes.  
"After years of studying, now I realize the truth—human melody aligns with the rules of the universe," sighed Lan He. 

Discussing all night long, they composed the "Winter Trio." The sections for pine and bamboo came naturally, except for the plum blossom section. They agreed to meet later to complete the plum blossom melody. 
As dawn approached and snow cleared, they parted, leaving the lingering echoes among the trees.

zh:
顾穿扬原是吴越顾氏旁支庶出，祖宗的荫蔽是享受不到多少了，只能靠自己去搏个前程。
他在能上马的年纪就从了军，凭一手骑射本事挣了个百夫长的位子。
他见识过战场上的尸山血海，也经历过军中的派系倾轧，他也因庶出身份处处受排挤。
烦透了。
顾穿扬什么都不要了，他只想找个清净地方待着，远离这些乱七八糟的东西。
如今他在临安学府当骑射教习，小萝卜头们的烦恼可比什么都有趣。当年在宗族和军中争得头破血流，如今只想安安生生待着。
顾穿扬哼着某首江南小调，晃晃悠悠往临安学府的大门走去。
“顾兄！”教辞赋的王夫子在身后叫住了他，“侬生病了，是伐？”
“要西快了，侬才生病了！”顾穿扬撩起袖子想展示下强壮的胳膊，就见王夫子冲上来捧起他的双手道：
“侬病的课都给了吴夫子，李夫子，我是一节课都没占到的呀！今朝，请侬病一下好伐？”话音未落，王夫子就冲进了学府大门，身后还跟着咬牙切齿的吴夫子。
顾穿扬手指着自己，看着这些书生为了抢课大打出手的样子，默默把话咽了回去。
这活计什么都好，就是……就是能不能少让他生点病？
en:
Gu Chuanyang was a concubine's son from a cadet branch of Wuyue's Gu clan. His family name didn't count for much. He would have to make his own way in the world.
He joined the army as soon as he was old enough to ride. His skill at mounted archery earned him the rank of Centurion.
He had seen the bloodshed of battle and endured the army's vicious power struggles. A concubine's son, he was pushed aside at every turn.
He'd had enough.
Gu Chuanyang no longer cared about any of it. He just wanted somewhere quiet, far away from the whole sorry mess.
Now he teaches mounted archery at Lin'an Academy, where nothing amuses him more than his young pupils' troubles. After fighting tooth and nail to get ahead in his clan and the army, he's content with a peaceful life.
Gu Chuanyang ambled toward the gates of Lin'an Academy, humming a Jiangnan tune.
"Gu!" Master Wang, who taught poetry and rhapsodies, called from behind him. "You're sick, aren't you?"
"Like hell I am! You're the sick one!" Gu Chuanyang pushed up his sleeves to show off his powerful arms, but Master Wang rushed over and clasped both his hands before he could.
"Your classes go to Master Wu and Master Li whenever you're sick. I haven't had a single one! Couldn't you be sick today, just for me?" Before he'd finished speaking, Master Wang charged through the academy gates, with Master Wu following behind, his teeth clenched in fury.
Gu Chuanyang pointed at himself and swallowed his retort as he watched the scholars come to blows over his classes.
Everything about the job suited him. It was just... well, couldn't they let him be sick a little less often?

【惊】梨园一弟子打尖不给钱，客栈老板不满：希望梨园加强常识教育！
近来，一梨园弟子外出游历，在客栈打尖却不带分文，妄图以一曲抵债。盘问之下，才知该弟子自小长在梨园避世，竟不知外面吃饭要花钱。客栈老板呼吁梨园加强弟子常识教育。截至目前，梨园尚未做出回应。
en:
[Warn] Spring Fever Spreads: Masked Troupe Reissues Love Ban!
Though Masked Troupe has always strictly forbidden romantic relationships among disciples, affections following spring fever bloom where they will. Lately, whispers of budding affection have stirred among younger members. In response, the sect has tightened patrols and once again issued a clear decree: No Romance Allowed!

[Thrill] Too Many Peepers! Taihu Lake Fish Demand Justice! Masked Troupe Must Take Full Responsibility.
According to an anonymous fish in Taihu Lake, no fewer than fifteen people have fallen into the lake this month while peeking Masked Troupe disciples rehearse. "It's all the Troupe's fault," the fish claims. "They're too charming and too reclusive. People can't help but peek. They should take full responsibility!"

[Shock] Masked Troupe Disciple Dines and Dashes. Innkeeper Denounces Their Basic Education!
A Masked Troupe disciple recently departed on a training journey and stopped at an inn without a single coin. Instead, he attempted to settle the bill with a song. Upon inquiry, it was revealed that the disciple had grown up entirely within the secluded grounds of the Masked Troupe and was unaware that food must be paid for outside. The innkeeper has since urged the Troupe to improve its disciples' basic knowledge of the outside world. As of now, the Troupe has yet to issue a response.

zh:
……没有长老愿帮助我们，都说没救了，认命吧，让那孩子解脱。
人只有一条命，若是“解脱”，便什么都没有了。
有一位姓张的学生听闻此事，说：墨经中的十二金人能舞能言，既然人的手脚能换，脑袋为何不能换？
真是疯子……但若想救这一条命，只能一试……由我们自己来试。
长老们说机关血肉是墨家禁术——那孩子不该活着。 我本以为张万师是个好脾气的人，却第一次看他那么生气。
这一年中，每每成长，连接处定如钝刀搓骨，疼痛难忍。张万师寻得麻沸散，但那孩子脾气倔强，宁肯嘶喊，不肯昏睡。
……我们真的做了一件好事吗？
年末，我们便要去墨山道了。往后这孩子的生死，谁也无法再预测。
离开前，青问我，山外的世界究竟如何？到底是怎样的世道会让一个孩子没有生路？
我无法回答……但我们都知道，山外的答案在山外，不在墨山道的学堂里。
en:
...No elder was willing to help us. They all said it was hopeless, to accept fate and let the child go.
A person has only one life. If we "die," there will be nothing left.
A student named Zhang heard about this and said: The twelve Golden Colossi in the Mohist Classic can dance and speak well. Since human hands and feet can be replaced, why not the head?
He's truly mad... But to save this one life, we had to try... by ourselves.
The elders say that mechanisms of flesh and blood are a Mohist forbidden art. That child shouldn't live. I thought Zhang Wanshi was good-tempered, but that was the first time I saw him so angry.
Throughout the year, whenever he grew, the connection points would grind against his bones like a blunt knife, the pain unbearable. Zhang Wanshi found Anesthesia Powder, but the child was stubborn, preferring to scream rather than sleep.
...Did we really do a good thing?
At the end of the year, we will go to Mohist Hill. From then on, no one can predict the child's life or death.
Before leaving, Halcyon asked me, what is the outside world really like? What kind of world would leave a child with no way to live?
I couldn't answer... But we all know that the answer outside the mountain lies outside the mountain, not in the classrooms of Mohist Hill.

开山以来的第一个清明，解忧司上下忙得饭也顾不上吃。
山里头一回来了这么多人，这才刚挨个提醒完要小心火烛，那儿又有人的行囊叫马猴给抢了去。慕名来寻春的人们带来了好些没见过的茶水点心，我们瞧着新鲜，马猴们也好奇得紧。这不，甄大哥去山上找马猴算账了，我才得空给游侠写下这封信。
忙点也好，总比闲着数云强。说起来，还得感谢游侠帮咱解忧司打响了名号，这些礼物，便是这些日子山里山外的人送来解忧司的。我和甄大哥就想着，给游侠也寄一点。清明天霁，游侠可拿去买些新茶点心，踏踏青，赏赏春。
得了空，也记得回山里看看！
en:
This first Qingming since the mountain was open has kept the Bureau of Relief so busy that we barely have time to sit down for a meal.
Never have so many folk come to the mountain at once. We had only just finished reminding everyone to be aware of the flames when word came in that a Macaque had snatched someone's travel pouch. Visitors who came to admire the Spring view brought all manner of teas and treats we had never seen—even the Macaques were curious. Zhen has gone up the mountain to settle the score with those monkeys, so I finally have a moment to write.
That said, being a little busy is a good thing. It's far better than sitting idly and counting clouds, at the very least. Come to think of it, we still owe you thanks for putting the Bureau of Relief on the map, Wanderer. These gifts are what the folk from in and around the mountain have sent our way lately. Zhen and I thought we ought to share some with you as well. The skies are clear this Qingming—perhaps you could treat yourself to some fresh tea and pastries, take a stroll through the verdant fields, and enjoy the spring.
Finally, if you find the time, do come back to the mountain for a visit!

zh:
十九岁那年，她跟着师父一行离开雾隐谷，来传闻中的机关之城不见山交流访学。

初至墨山道，她对山中那些精妙的榫卯机巧充满了好奇。
飞空的木鸢，推地的木螂，报时的仪象，通天的悬撞……还有天陉上那处适宜观测星象的好地方！
虽离了家，星子仍悬于高空，抬头便能仰望。

原来在雾隐谷外，在隐世的不见山里，也有那么多好奇于算学、又憧憬着无垠星空的人。
她同他们一起在浮英野漫天的花海里，一夜连一夜地观测，兴致勃勃地将所究之理分享给每一个仰望星斗的人。

访学期满，那些曾同她一起来不见山讲学论道的同门都已离开，独她仍沉迷在测绘中，长留此地，当起了算学和观星的先生。
待回过神来，她已在这儿结识了诸多同好，亦有人得其授业称她作老师。再后来，她又在这里安了家。

只是这星星啊，看得见，却够不着的，去追它做什么？就像那些乘着风飞向星斗的人，她也总够不着。
不过人呐，就是这样，明知追不着，也总忍不住跑两步，踮踮脚，便是如今老了，常记不得路，仍不自觉往家门外溜——还是去追星星。

诶？真的就没够着吗？

她愣了愣，粗糙枯槁的手里，正攥着一只柔软的小手，旁边的小姑娘正絮絮叨叨说个不停。
这是往哪走呢？哦，对了，这是往家走呢。
小月鹿，小月鹿，这是奶奶的小月鹿。

“小月鹿啊，你还记得你小时候哭闹，我们是怎么哄你的吗？”
“用星星？”
“对咯！奶奶小时候有根星子鱼竿，你也有一根。可惜啊，真的星星，咱们够不着咧。”
“星星不是够不着的，奶奶真糊涂。话本子里不是说了吗？云中君摘下星子分给了世人，大家就都有了自己的星星。奶奶要是不信，我也可以送奶奶很多很多星星。”

小月鹿又在家里准备了许多“星星”？这一次是二十八宿，还是北斗星辰？

不过这一次是小月鹿说得对，奶奶这一辈子，有过许多星星了。

她轻轻捏了捏小月鹿的小手——现在手里的，就是奶奶最亮的那颗星星啊。

奶奶够着咧。
en:
At nineteen, she followed her master and the others out of Mist-Hidden Vale and came to Hidden Mountain, the famed city of mechanisms, on a visiting exchange.
When she first arrived on Mohist Hill, she was fascinated by the ingenious mortise-and-tenon devices scattered through the mountain. There were wooden eagles that soared through the air, wooden scarabs that scuttled along the ground, instruments that marked the hours, sky-reaching suspended structures... and, above all, that wonderful spot on Heaven's Threshold! where the stars could be observed.

She had left home, yet the stars were still there overhead. All she had to do was lift her eyes.
Only then did she realize that beyond Mist-Hidden Vale, within the secluded Hidden Mountain, there were so many others who were just as drawn to mathematics and just as filled with wonder for the boundless night sky.
Together they spent night after night amid the sea of blossoms at Driftseed Moor, watching the heavens and eagerly sharing what they had learned with everyone who looked up at the stars.

When her time of study came to an end, the fellow disciples who had come with her to lecture and exchange ideas all left Hidden Mountain. She alone stayed behind, still absorbed in observation and charting, and in time became a teacher of mathematics and astronomy.
Before she knew it, she had found many kindred spirits there, and some who studied under her had even begun to call her Master. Later still, she made her home there.

And yet, those stars... you can see them, but you cannot touch them, so why keep chasing after them? Just like those who rode the wind toward the stars, they always seemed beyond her reach.
But people are like that. Even when they know they will never catch what they chase, they still cannot help but run a few steps more, rise onto their toes, and try anyway. Even now, old as she was, often forgetting the way, she would still wander out the door without thinking, still chasing the stars.

Eh? Had she really never reached them?
She paused.
In her rough, weathered hand was a small, soft one, and beside her the little girl kept chattering away.

Where were they headed again? Ah, right. They were on their way home.
Yuelu. Yuelu. This was Granny's Yuelu.

"Yuelu, do you remember how we used to soothe you when you cried as a child?"
"With stars?"
"That's right. Granny had a star-fishing rod when she was little, and you have one too. Shame we can't really reach the real stars."
"Of course we can, Granny. You're being silly. Doesn't it say so in the storybooks? The Lord of Clouds plucked down stars and shared them with the world, so everyone got a star of their own. If you don't believe me, I can give you lots and lots of stars too."
Had Yuelu prepared more "stars" at home again? Would it be the Twenty-Eight Mansions this time, or the stars of the Northern Dipper?

But this time, Yuelu was right.
Granny had already had many stars in her life.
She gently squeezed Yuelu's little hand. The one in her hand now was Granny's brightest star of all.

This time, Granny had reached one.
