#Y记：君子不变节从俗，纵身死受戮亦不改其心。言此，吾师怅然，久立无言，竟有呜咽声……
高辛者，古之圣人也。玄鸟致诒即求娶简狄也。此非言婚配，乃是以求女喻思君。凡求女，必香草罗怀，高歌往之。佩香草以求女，实云洁德行求明君也，纵历年久，罹难遭辱，亦不移也。#E
en:
The ethereal spirit of Gaoxin flourished. He sent the Mystic Bird bearing gifts.
I wished to change my ways and follow the common custom, yet I was ashamed to abandon my resolve and bend my will.
Alone I passed the years in sorrow and hardship, yet my heart remained unchanged.

—Qu Yuan, "Longing for the Fair One"

#YAnnotation: A gentleman does not change his ways to follow common custom. Even should he meet death and suffer slaughter, he will not alter his heart. When my master spoke these words, he fell into a long melancholy, standing in silence for a great while, until at last there came a sound of quiet weeping...
Gaoxin was a Sage of antiquity. The Mystic Bird bearing gifts refers to the wooing of Jian Di. Yet this is not truly speech of marriage. It is an allegory of longing for one's lord, spoken through the seeking of a woman. In common courtship, one must carry fragrant herbs at one's breast and go forth singing. To bear a pendant of fragrant herbs in seeking the beloved is in truth to speak of pursuing a wise and enlightened ruler through pure virtue and conduct, and to hold to that, unwavering, through years of hardship and humiliation alike.#E

zh:
显德五年四月廿五，我和林澜说定了，这次回来后就再也不出海了。
这些年攒的钱，加上客商说好的报酬，够买涌泉镇外一片荒地。我先拿了一笔定金，换了几只小羊，小鱼很喜欢。
林澜问我：“明年也不出海了？”她是掌舵弄舟的好手，比起我总离海更亲近些。
我说：“种地看天，总比看海强。羊也好养，等来年生一窝，年景再差也饿不着。”
海里的日子太长了。每次放洋，船摇在浪里，天连水水连天，四周什么都没有，只有风声和浪声。你不知道船底下什么时候翻出大鱼，也不知道天边什么时候涌起乌云。
这些年出海的人，十个回来七个就算好的了。鱼信姑的丈夫就是去年走的，船翻了，尸骨都没找着。
我想，小鱼讨厌水，那就离水远点吧。等搬到涌泉镇，她可以放羊割草，可以去蒙学读书。我们会有一座小院，在里面给她讲故事。
我把这些说给林澜听，也说起那些客商的可疑。传说只是传说，我当传说讲，也当传说听——世界上怎么会真的有那样一艘宝船呢？那些人为何要找那艘宝船呢？
林澜低头织着网，说：“我奶奶出海的时候，见过那艘宝船下海；我娘出海的时候，见过那艘宝船在海上漂。你奶奶也见过的，你娘也知道的，你也讲过的。”
她还是想要出海，想要找到宝船，我好像又看到了我娘，她给我讲宝船的事时，也是这样的神情。
四月廿七，我跟柳姨家换了只种羊，瘦归瘦，看着还精神。小鱼高兴得天天围着羊圈转，给每只羊都起了名字。
四月三十，出海前夜，小鱼央着林澜讲八仙过海的故事。林澜讲的故事和镇上戏台上讲的都不同，她的故事会变，这次故事里有了羊，她说我们会骑着羊，找到宝船，到蓬莱山上。
小鱼听完了故事，依旧不肯睡觉，不停地问我们什么时候回来，吵着要我们给个准话。
我说，一个月后肯定回来，到时候给你买更多的小羊。我们和小鱼拉了勾，算作立了契书，小鱼才心满意足地睡了。
次日我和林澜一大早就出发了，尽量放轻手脚，没吵着小鱼。
走到海边，我回头看了一眼。小鱼不知什么时候跑到了屋子门口，远远朝我挥手。羊挤在她身边咩咩叫着，像天上的云。
船五月初一辰时三刻开。我和林澜五月初一辰时一刻上船。
写于五月初一申时二刻。
en:
The twenty-fifth day of the fourth month, the fifth year of Xiande. I agreed with Lin Lan that after returning from this trip, we would never set sail again. The money we have saved over these years, combined with the payment promised by the merchants, is enough to buy a patch of wasteland outside Wellspring Town. I took a portion of the deposit first and traded it for a few small goats. Xiaoyu loves them.
Lin Lan asked me, "You really won't sail next year?" She is an expert at the helm and handling boats, always feeling closer to the sea than I do.
I replied, "Farming depends on the heavens, but it is still better than depending on the sea. Goats are easy to raise, too. When they give birth to a litter next year, we won't go hungry even if the harvest is poor."
The days at sea are far too long. Every time we sail out into the open ocean, the ship rocks in the waves. The sky meets the water, and the water meets the sky; there is nothing around us but the sound of the wind and the surf. You never know when a massive fish might breach beneath the hull, nor when dark clouds might surge on the horizon. Among those who have gone to sea these past years, returning seven out of ten is considered a blessing. Aunt Yuxin's husband departed last year; his ship capsized, and his bones were never found.
I figured, since Xiaoyu hates the water, we should stay far away from it. Once we move to Wellspring Town, she can herd goats, cut grass, and attend the local academy. We will have a small courtyard where we can tell her stories.
I told Lin Lan all of this, and also mentioned how suspicious those merchants seemed. Legends are just legends. I speak of them as tales, and I listen to them as tales. For how could such a treasure ship truly exist in this world? Why are those people searching for it?
Lin Lan lowered her head, weaving a net, and said, "When my grandmother went to sea, she saw that treasure ship set sail; when my mother went to sea, she saw it drifting on the waves. Your grandmother saw it too, your mother knew of it, and you yourself have spoken of it."
She still wants to go to sea; she still wants to find the Treasure Ship. I seemed to see my mother again; she had the exact same look in her eyes when she told me about the ship.
The twenty-seventh day of the fourth month. I traded for a breeding ram from Auntie Liu's family. It is thin, but looks spirited enough. Xiaoyu is so thrilled she circles the shed every day, giving every single goat a name.
The thirtieth day of the fourth month, the night before we sail. Xiaoyu begged Lin Lan to tell the story of the Eight Immortals crossing the sea. Lin Lan's version is always different from the ones told on the town stages. Her stories change. This time, there were goats in the tale. She said we would ride the goats, find the Treasure Ship, and travel to Mount Penglai.
After hearing the story, Xiaoyu still refused to sleep, endlessly asking when we would return, fussing until we gave her a firm answer. I told her we would definitely be back in a month, and I would buy her even more small goats. We locked pinkies with Xiaoyu, treating it as a binding contract. Only then did she fall asleep, fully satisfied.
The next morning, Lin Lan and I set out bright and early, moving as quietly as possible so as not to wake Xiaoyu.
As we reached the shore, I looked back. I do not know when she ran to the doorway, but Xiaoyu was waving at me from afar. The goats huddled around her, bleating, looking just like clouds in the sky.
The ship sails at the third quarter of the Chen Hour on the first day of the fifth month. Lin Lan and I boarded at the first quarter of the Chen Hour.
Written at the second quarter of the Shen Hour, on the first day of the fifth month.

zh:
《春醪独抚》

她初至梨园，先见到一片桃花林，听到一阵乐声。

桃夭灼灼，她在树与花的迷阵里不知方向，只能循着乐声往深处走。往深处走，人影渐明。她低头避开一根枝桠，抬头时春风拂面，有舞者如一片落英翩然飞到她的面前。

“你会唱歌吗？”舞者问。
“会一点。”
“那来给我伴唱吧！”

舞者捉着她的手腕往台上跑，足尖一点就飞到枝头。
“来呀！唱！”

她茫然地开口，舞者随她的歌声扬袖旋身，于花树间轻盈徘徊。花与人，人与花，交织成绮丽的梦影。
于是她迟疑的歌声唱得越来越定、越来越亮，和舞者的步履宛转相合。

一曲终了。她尚且怔愣，舞者已经蝴蝶般投入她怀中，笑道：“我喜欢你！你叫什么名字？”
“我入梨园，是为了抛却过往……就叫白新。”
“刚取的吗？真好听！我叫阿朱，待你入门，来跟我合演好不好？”
“……好。”

这是她们合演的第一曲，唯有天地山水看见。
很快，就有了第二曲、第三曲……越来越多的人看见她们的歌舞，越来越多的人喜欢她们的歌舞。
阿朱的舞以繁复华美为要，她的歌以轻灵无垢称道，合演之时，既是彼此互补，又是默契天成。梨园内遂称她们为一时双璧。

园中舞乐不休，岁月白驹在技艺精研中奔驰得飞快。
第二年春天，她们在相遇的桃花树下埋了一坛酒，约定冬日再来启封。
夏蝉鸣叫的时候，她们各自遇到了技艺的瓶颈。
秋季的某一日，阿朱飞到她窗前，眼神明亮地说：“我想到了！我想到要如何突破如今的困境了！”
“舞是世间万千生灵共通的话语。倘若没有见过世间的万千生灵如何在山河间漫游，我怎么能够舞出其中的神韵呢？我决定了，我要到外面去。去见山、见水、见众生！”
“你要随我一起走吗？”

“不了。”她摇摇头，“世间百声繁杂，会有碍我想表达的声音。”

她的蝴蝶飞走了。
但她并不伤心。
她觉得相遇与重逢都是理所应当的事情，告别之后，自然会有重聚。谁也没有觉得不舍。她们理应走上自己认定的道路，成为更好的人以后重逢，再一起完成更完美的歌舞。

直到有一日，新进的弟子问她，“您有见过朱大家的舞吗？朱大家以舞姿纷繁、如揽万象于舞中而闻名；您的歌喉则纯澈灵粹、脱俗于世外，若能乐舞同台，一定会像两块碧玉一样相映成辉！”
她才恍然惊觉，已经有许多许多年，没有见过阿朱了。

她去找当年埋的春酒，却遍寻不到一片桃夭灼灼的花林。
梨园当真有一片桃花林吗？还是那一日的记忆太鲜妍，以至于也为记忆中的花卉着色？
她不记得了。甚至不记得，是否真有那样一个蝴蝶般的人、一场如梦般的歌舞。
那一日的天与地、山和水还记得吗？

她去沽了一壶酒，一人两杯，望着天边的行云饮完了。
en:
A Solo Serenade in Spring 

When she first stepped into the Masked Troupe, her eyes were greeted by a blooming grove of peach trees, and soft music floated through the air. 

Amid the radiant blossoms, she found herself lost in a labyrinth of petals and branches, unsure of the way—but she followed the melody deeper into the grove. As she ventured further, shadows of figures began to emerge. Bending to dodge a low-hanging branch, she looked up just as a spring breeze brushed her cheek, and a dancer, as light and graceful as falling petals, twirled down to meet her. 

"Can you sing?" the dancer asked with a smile. 
"A little." 
"Then sing with me." 

Seizing her wrist, the dancer led her toward the stage, then, with a delicate tap of toes, soared onto a branch above. 
"Come on! Sing!" 

At first hesitant, her voice gradually grew steadier and clearer, weaving seamlessly with the dancer's flowing movements. Between the blossoms and their intertwined forms, the two became a living dream of music and motion. 
Her tentative melody blossomed into a confident, radiant song, perfectly echoing the dancer's elegant steps. 

When the final note faded, she was still caught in the moment, while the dancer, fluttering like a butterfly, leapt into her arms and laughed, "I like you! What's your name?" 
"I came to the Masked Troupe to leave my past behind... Call me Bai Xin." 
"Did you just choose that? It's beautiful. I'm A'zhu. When you officially join, will you perform with me?" 
"...Yes." 

Their first duet was witnessed only by the sky, the earth, and the murmuring mountains. 
Soon came a second, then a third... and more and more people gathered to behold and be enchanted by their singing and dancing. 
A'zhu's dance dazzled with intricate grace and brilliance; Bai Xin's voice shimmered with lightness and purity. Together, their performances were a perfect harmony of contrast and complement—so natural it seemed destined. They were celebrated in the Masked Troupe as an unparalleled pair. 

Music and dance filled the garden day and night, and the years swiftly passed as their artistry deepened. 
The following spring, beneath the very peach tree where they first met, they buried a jar of wine, promising to return and open it together when winter came again. 
When the summer cicadas sang their endless chorus, both of them found themselves trapped in the stubborn grip of a creative block. 
One crisp autumn day, A'zhu appeared at her window, eyes bright with sudden realization. "I've figured it out! I know how to break free from this rut!" 
"Dance is the universal language of all living things. Without witnessing the countless creatures that roam the mountains and rivers, how could I ever capture their spirit in my movement? I've made up my mind—I must go beyond these walls. I'll see the landscape and all the living souls out there!" 
"Will you come with me?" 

"No," she answered softly, shaking her head. "The world is filled with clamorous sounds that would drown out the voice I'm trying to hear." 

And with that, her butterfly took flight and vanished on the breeze. 
Yet she felt no sorrow. 
To her, meetings and partings were natural cycles, inevitable and necessary. Farewells only made reunions sweeter. There was no room for clinging; each was meant to walk the path their heart knew best—to become more fully themselves—until they could once again join in song and dance, more perfect than ever before. 

Then one day, a new disciple asked her, "Have you ever seen Master Zhu's dance? She weaves the universe itself into her movements. Your voice, pure and transcendent, soars beyond the everyday. If your music and her dance graced the same stage, it would be like two jade gems reflecting each other's brilliance." 
It was then she realized with a pang—how many long years had passed since she last saw A'zhu? 

She returned to the place where they'd buried their spring wine, but found no sign of the radiant peach grove they once called home. 
Did the Masked Troupe ever truly bloom with peach blossoms? Or had that day's memory simply painted its own dreamlike flowers? 
She no longer knew. She couldn't say if there had ever truly been that butterfly-like figure, or that ethereal song and dance. 
But perhaps the sky and earth remembered—the mountains and rivers. 

She bought a jar of wine, poured two cups, and raising them to the drifting clouds on the horizon, drank alone—a quiet toast to what was, and what might still be.

张错永远记得，与冯如之擦肩而过的那一刻。
浊浪滔天，怒风呼啸，没能说动赤龙的青蛟，离开了黄河，去寻找属于自己的江流。
这是张错第二次离开被称作“家”的地方。

上一次还是童稚之时，一觉醒来，家中便只剩下自己一个了。记忆碎片里，是狭窄的洞穴、无光的暗道、不伸舌头便啜饮不到的岩隙水和……腥臭的鼠肉。好不容易逃出生天的自己只记得洞口那一只小小的手，在光里拼命晃着，像在为自己呼唤光明。
那是张错和冯如之第一次碰面，结局其实并不愉快：每年生辰，冯如之都会念起当年的小野兽狠狠的一口。但还好也没有太坏，张错早已习惯熟稔地别过脸，在众人的哄笑中，咳嗽着饮下一杯“红袖招”陈酒。
“你咬回来。”
“下次一定。”
en:
Zhang Cuo would never forget the moment he brushed past Feng Ruzhi.
The waves raged, the winds howled, but the azure flood dragon could not persuade the crimson dragon. 
It left the Yellow River to seek its own waters.
This was the second time Zhang Cuo left the place he once called "home."

The first time was during his childhood. When he woke up, the house was empty, just him, all alone. His fragmented memories were of a narrow cave, pitch-black tunnels, water seeping through rocky cracks that he could only lap up with his tongue, and the stench of raw rat meat. After barely escaping alive, all he remembered was a small hand at the cave's entrance, waving desperately in the light, as though summoning brightness for him.
That was his first meeting with Feng Ruzhi. It didn't end well. Every year on Feng Ruzhi's birthday, she would jokingly recall the feral little creature that had bitten her hard back then. At least it wasn't all bad. By now, Zhang Cuo had learned to turn away gracefully, coughing as he downed a cup of the notorious "Red Sleeve Special" amidst everyone's laughter.
"Why don't you bite back?"
"Next time, for sure."

至于第三事……等我完成了这两事再告诉我。

而今，边陲阡陌之间，百姓今年新种之苗已初现新绿，凉州亦再复归。承托的二事均已办妥，您未说的第三事……到底是什么？

Uncle,
Twelve years have passed since our secret talk in the Buddhist shrine that night.
You said to me then, "Huaishen, since you have taken up this banner, there are three behests I must entrust to you." I agreed without hesitation, believing that if I fought with all my might, nothing in this world would be beyond my reach.

#YThe first was to ensure the people are fed and clothed. The second, to safeguard the frontier's peace.#E
We agreed that upon a bountiful year, we would forge a bronze Harvest Tribute and send it to Chang'an. You said #Yfour beasts#E would suffice for the tribute, wishing to spare the remaining bronze for the people to forge farming tools.
As for the third behest... you told me to complete the first two before you would reveal it.

Now, fresh green shoots are sprouting across the borderlands, and Liangzhou has been fully restored. The first two behests you entrusted to me are done. What exactly is the third?

我的孩子：

我的小小侠客，马上，你就要踏上一个人的冒险了。
你会翻过一座座山，跨过一道道河，马车会带你去到很远很远的地方。别害怕，那里有和家里一样好看的月亮，你会见到许多陌生的风景，有意思的人们。
娘多想和你一块儿去，好告诉你哪里的风光更好一些，哪条路更好走一些。
可娘也有自己的冒险。娘要走的路很难，很远，娘可能永远也走不到尽头，也可能什么也阻挡不了。但只要想到还能拉着小春和的手，再回到滹沱河边散步，一起数水里的月亮，娘就必须要去试一试。
娘知道，咱们春和自小胆子就大。可这次要答应娘，这一路上要好好听于叔的话，不要太轻易相信旁人，若遇上了坏人也千万不要逞强。
别的事娘都交代给于叔了。等到春天来了，树叶绿了，坏人都被打跑了，娘就去南边找你们。到时候，再把你这一路上的冒险，好好跟娘讲讲。
en:
My child,

My little hero, before long you will be setting out on an adventure of your own.
You will cross mountain after mountain, ford river after river, and the carriage will carry you to places far, far away. Do not be afraid. The moon there is just as beautiful as the one at home, and you will see many unfamiliar sights, and meet many interesting people.
How I wish I could go with you, to tell you which views are loveliest, and which roads are easier to take.
But I have an adventure of her own. The road I must take is hard, and long. I may never reach its end, or perhaps nothing will be able to stand in my way. But as long as I can still hope to take you by the hand again, to return to the banks of the Hutuo River for a walk, and count the moons in the water together, then I must try.
Chunhe, I know that you're a brave child. But this time, you must promise me this: on the journey, listen carefully to Uncle Yu, do not trust strangers too easily, and if you encounter bad people, do not try to be brave all by yourself.
As for everything else, I've already entrusted it to Uncle Yu. When spring comes, when the leaves turn green, and all the bad people have been driven away, I will come south to find you. When that time comes, you must tell me all about the adventures you had along the way.

But in that pavilion, she saw a chess set left behind by someone unknown. In the long and repetitive days as a palace maid, she never imagined she could also take on the identity of a player. She easily became captivated by the game. The senior maid was understanding; as long as Mingqi finished her duties, she would turn a blind eye to her sneaking off to play.
Outside the palace, dynasties rise and fall. Within the crimson walls, only the players change. Female officials, civil ministers, imperial consorts... Could there ever come a day when Mingqi, as a mere pawn, captures the general?

zh:
月鹿归山，随信一封。弟子奚怀，罪愆深重，惶恐不知从何书起。

为保堪绘舆图之精确详实，吾师风叙常不避险峻，亲身跋涉于太行崎岖险壑之间。那日风急，至三更忽起夜雨，吾师上山迟迟未归，弟子冒雨相寻。至天明，方据泥泞足印，寻至一崖边。得崖上滑痕，方知师已失足坠山。山崖险急，无处下之，不得再寻。
后于吾师案前得手稿一卷，书至半途，似有疑窦，想是欲于启程前夜求证一二，匆匆上山，方遇此难。
吾师溘然，弟子实难自释。世事无常，天意何诘？唯吾师未竟之业，弟子当以死继之。

自吾师去后，月鹿大病一场，此皆弟子看顾之失。
辗转再三，幸得鸦先生相助，将月鹿送归山中。山间清宁，月鹿定能安然成长，也盼与二老作伴，承欢膝下，得一牵挂。

叩首请罪，恕弟子无能，未护吾师周全。墨山道及书院之恩，弟子没齿难忘。来日书成，并一应所得献与墨门，聊表寸心。再拜。
en:
As Yuelu returns to the mountains, I send this letter with her. My heart is heavy with guilt, and I hardly know where to begin.

To ensure that the maps she drew were exact and complete, my master, Feng Xu, never shrank from danger, but crossed the steep ridges and perilous ravines of the Taihang Mountains in person. That day, the wind blew hard. Around midnight, a storm appeared out of nowhere. Still, my master had not returned from the mountain. I went out into the storm to search for her. Only at daybreak, following the tracks left in the mud, did I reach the edge of a cliff. There I found the marks of a slip, and at last, understood that my master had lost her footing and fallen down the mountainside. The cliff was sheer and treacherous, with no way down. I could search no farther.
Afterward, on my master's desk, I found a half-written manuscript. It broke off midway, as though some doubt had arisen in her mind. I believe she meant to verify a point or two before setting out, and in her haste climbed the mountain that very night, only to meet this calamity.
My master's sudden death is a grief I cannot lay down. The affairs of this world are ever uncertain. By what justice does Heaven ordain such things? Only this much is certain: the work my master left unfinished, I shall carry on even at the cost of my life.
After my master's death, Yuelu fell gravely ill. This too was my failure in caring for her.
After many difficulties, and with Master Raven's help, I have at last sent Yuelu back to the mountain. She will surely grow up safe and well among its tranquility. I also hope she may keep the two of you company, and bring you some comfort in your later years.
Forgive me. I failed to keep my master safe. The kindness shown to me by Mohist Hill and the academy alike is something I shall never forget. When the book is finished, I will offer it, along with all I have learned, to Mohist Hill as a token of my gratitude.

With deepest respects...

zh:
奉国都虞候王清将军 钧鉴

狂澜举义于西北，闻晋师与契丹相持滹沱，特率部突围南下，愿助将军一臂之力，共破虏人。
素闻杜重威将军持节秉钺，威重令严，时某人微言轻，若径自上书陈表琐事，恐扰视听。故烦请王清将军代转数言。

夫行军者，不过三要：兵、马、粮草也。
狂澜既号义军，人心自附，兵源不劳朝廷筹计。为求灵活策应、临机决断，便请我部自为一军，而后应尽之事不再一一隶呈。如此，纵使或有奸通契丹、泄露军机之虞，我军犹为大局存一转圜余地。
此番南下，转战折损，骑乘多数尽殒。时某知杜将军亦爱惜良骏，厩中多蓄宝马战驹。常言道：“好马不停蹄，好牛不停犁。”今事急矣，且由义军先行取用，以充骑乘。杜将军藏器待时，何如义军应时而动？
滹沱对峙，恐成久战。义军不比朝廷仓禀丰足，粮饷之筹实为至要。杜将军深谋远虑，为大军预储私财甚厚，若得此助，购粮一事当不足为虑。时某且先行寻取，待物资到手，再来仔细谢过将军。

近日城关内外，多见绘有时某形貌之告示文书。杜将军如此抬爱，某诚惶惶。奈何如今契丹未破，岂敢言赏？待他日克竟全功，自当亲赴帐前，向将军请领酬勋。
en:
To General Wang Qing, Commander of the Fengguo Army,

Raging Tides has raised the banner of righteousness in the northwest. Hearing that the Jin army stands locked against the Khitans at the Hutuo River, I have led my men south in breakout, hoping to lend you my strength and join you in breaking the northern foe.
I have long heard that Du Chongwei holds tally and axe in hand, with weighty authority and stern command. A man such as I is of little standing and slighter voice. Were I to trouble him directly with these few words, I fear they would never reach his ear. I therefore ask that you pass them on for me.

In the art of war, there are but three essentials: soldiers, steeds, and rations.

As Raging Tides commands a righteous host, men gather to us of their own accord, and the court need not spend thought on raising troops for our sake. For the sake of swift response and timely action, I ask only that my force be allowed to stand apart as an army unto itself, without every matter being tied up in reports and petitions. Thus, even if there are those in high command who traffic with the Khitans and let military secrets slip abroad, there may yet remain some room to salvage the greater situation.

In this southward march, after many battles and losses, most of our mounts have perished. I know that Du Chongwei is a great lover of fine horses, and that his stables hold many worthy chargers. As the saying goes, a good horse does not idle in the stable, nor a good ox stand idle from the plough. The moment is urgent. Let the righteous army put those horses to use first and replenish our cavalry. Better that they carry men into battle than remain hidden away waiting on Du Chongwei's leisure.
At the Hutuo River, the armies stand opposed, and this is likely to become a long war. A righteous army is not like the court, with overflowing storehouses and deep reserves. Grain and pay are matters of life and death. Yet Du Chongwei, in his admirable foresight, has already laid by no small wealth for the army's future needs. If that treasure may be put to proper use, then provisions will be no cause for worry. I shall go first and see it found. Once supplies are in hand, I will return and offer him my thanks in full.

In recent days, both within and beyond the passes, I have often seen notices bearing my likeness. Such favor from Du Chongwei leaves me deeply moved. Yet while the Khitans remain unbroken, how could I dare speak of reward? When victory is won, I shall present myself before his tent in person and receive his generosity then.
But... that was a long time ago...

en:
From the very beginning, Li Zhenzhen used her own hands to explore the world. 
To feel her way forward, to block the blades before her, to stain herself with the blood that could not be avoided. 
In time, her hands became bruised, rough, calloused, and ugly. 

Later, the one and only friend she ever had gave her this pair of gauntlets. 
May you be like this silk, pure as the moon behind the clouds,
untouched by the dust of the world. 

She had always left the gift where it was. 
After all, when a gift carries a hope you can't fulfill, it becomes too heavy to lift.

对芦花来说，春天是个看不见的客人。

“娘，春天长什么样？”芦花歪着脑袋问。
娘愣了一下，用冻得通红的手往火堆里填了几把芦苇草，火苗噼啪噼啪把娘的脸也照得通红。娘说：“等冰化了，鱼跳出水面，鸟飞回来，芦苇变绿了，春天就来了。”
鸟，就是在天上飞来飞去的，她看得见；鱼，就是在水底下甩着尾巴的，她看得见；芦苇，就是被风吹起一层又一层的浪，她也看得见。
可春天，到底长什么样子呢？娘还是没有说。
所以在芦花心里，春天像个远道而来的客人，只在暖和的时候悄悄来一趟。来时带着鱼、带着鸟、带着一整片绿油油的芦苇，能让娘少咳几声，让她的肚子少空几顿。
“要是这个客人，能待久一点就好了。”
芦花缩在火边，蹭蹭狗哥乱糟糟的毛，这样想着。
因为冬天，实在太冷了。
是手上张开的小嘴会咬人，划桨的时候，手指一弯就疼。是鼻子里会流下眼泪；是冻得梆梆硬的衣服，和一到夜里就跟着打哆嗦的屋子。
她这么和娘说的时候，娘笑着告诉芦花，娘小时候的冬天，只有白的山，黑的水，比这还要冷，还要难熬。但“熬过去就好了……等冰化了的时候，河水会带着春天来的。”

只是今年的冬天，好像比往年的更长。
先是鸟走了。它们一队一队的，从水面飞起来，绕着芦苇荡盘了几圈，最后一头扎向远处灰白色的天。
芦花拉了拉娘的袖子：“娘，它们去哪儿呀？”
“往暖和的地方去。”娘望着那片天，眼神跟着飞出去，半晌才落回来，“来年春天就回来了。”
再是，人也走了。
她看见村里的人也像鸟一样，一队接一队的，背着东西，划着船走了。有人路过芦苇荡，会远远地朝她和娘喊上两句，娘只是摇摇头。
“娘，他们去哪儿呀？”芦花问。
“往暖和的地方去。”娘还是这个回答，只是嗓子有些哑了。
再后来，河结了冰。
她趴在河沿上往下看，只看见冰底下一片灰蒙蒙，鱼不见了，网拉上来是空的，只有冰碴和冻僵的芦苇根。
“鱼也去暖和的地方了吗？”
这回，没有人回答芦花的问题了，只有风呼呼地吹过芦苇。因为娘出去了，一直没回来呢。

咔嚓——河面上的冰裂了一道缝。
噗通——像是有鱼跳出了水面，又很快没了影子。

是春天回来了吗？是那个看不见的客人，顺着河水来了吗？它是不是把娘也一块带回来了？芦花不知道。

但她知道，只要熬过冬天，总会等来春天的。
en:
To Luhua, spring was an invisible guest.

"Mom, what does spring look like?" she asked, tilting her head.
Her mother paused for a moment, then tossed a few handfuls of reed grass into the fire with hands reddened by the cold. The flames crackled and lit up her face as well.
"When the ice melts," her mother said, "when the fish start jumping, the birds come back, and the reeds turn green, that's when spring comes."

Birds were the things flying across the sky. Those she could see.
Fish were the things flicking their tails under the water. Those she could see too.
And the reeds were the ones that rippled in layer after layer when the wind blew. Those she could see as well.
But what did spring itself look like? Her mother still hadn't said.

So in Luhua's mind, spring was like a guest from far away, slipping in quietly when the weather turned warm.
It came with fish, with birds, and with whole stretches of green reeds. It made her mother cough a little less, and it meant fewer days with an empty belly.

"If only this guest could stay a little longer."
Curled up by the fire, rubbing against the dog's messy fur, Luhua thought just that.
Because winter was just too cold.

It was the little cracks in her hands, split open like tiny mouths that bit when she moved. It was the pain in her fingers whenever they bent around an oar. It was her runny nose, the stiff frozen clothes, and the house that seemed to shiver along with her once night fell.

When she said this to her mother, her mother would smile and tell her that the winters of her own childhood had been nothing but white mountains and black waters, colder than this, harder to endure.
"But once you make it through, you'll be fine. When the ice melts, the river will bring spring with it."

Only this year, winter seemed longer than usual.

First the birds left.
They rose from the water flock after flock, circled over the reeds a few times, then plunged into the gray-white sky in the distance.

Luhua tugged at her mother's sleeve. "Mom, where are they going?"
"Somewhere warm."
Her mother kept looking at the sky, her gaze following them far off before it finally came back.
"They'll return next spring."

Then the people left too.
Luhua watched the villagers go the same way as the birds, group after group, rowing away with their things on their backs. Sometimes someone passing the reeds would call out a few words from afar, and her mother would only shake her head.

"Mom, where are they going?" Luhua asked.
"Somewhere warm."
It was the same answer as before, only now her mother's voice had grown hoarse.

Later, the river froze over.
Luhua lay by the riverbank and looked down, but all she could see beneath the ice was a dull gray blur. The fish were gone. Whenever she pulled up the net, it came back empty, with nothing in it but ice chips and frozen reed roots.
"Did the fish go somewhere warm too?"

This time, no one answered her.
Only the wind rushed through the reeds.
Her mother had gone out, and still hadn't come back.

Crack.
A split opened across the frozen river.
Splash.
Something seemed to leap out of the water, like a fish, and then it was gone again.

Was spring back?
Had that invisible guest come drifting in with the river?
Had it brought her mother back too?

Luhua didn't know.
But she did know this: if you could just make it through winter, spring would come in the end.

游侠，近来可好啊？我听墨门弟子说，你走山访水，开拓产业，定然遇到了不少奇人异事吧。光是想想，就让人心头痒痒。
我这边呢，昨日帮孙家小子翻墙捡木鸢，前日满街追着徐婶子的鸡跑，再往前数……总之还是老样子。这刀闷在刀鞘里，指不定哪日就生锈了。总想着，什么时候能遇上一桩大案，追凶千里、拔剑破局的那种！
嘿嘿，所以我左思右想，想到了游侠你，没有人比你更靠谱了。你经历的事多，路子也广，只要跟着你，就一定能碰上奇事。你放心，我会拿出看家本领，绝不给你拖后腿。甄捕头那你不用担心，我会说服他给我批这个假的！
en:
Wanderer, how have you been lately? I heard from a Mohist disciple that you've been traveling far and wide, opening up new ventures. You must have run into your share of strange people and stranger affairs. Just thinking about it makes my fingers itch.
As for me, yesterday I helped the Sun family's boy climb a wall to fetch his wooden eagle. The day before, I was running all over the streets chasing Aunt Xu's chicken. And before that... well, more of the same. This blade has sat in its sheath so long it may rust one day. I keep hoping for a real case, the kind where you hunt the culprit for a thousand miles and draw your sword to break the deadlock.
So I got to thinking, and of course I thought of you, Wanderer. No one is more reliable. You've seen more than most and your connections run wide. If I follow you, I'm bound to come across something worth my while. Rest easy, I'll bring my best and I won't slow you down. As for Constable Zhen, don't worry. I'll talk him into approving my leave.

zh: 毛天佑自小便喜静。不知是不是受了他那沉默寡言的父亲毛乙的影响，在同龄人都上蹿下跳的年纪，毛天佑最爱的，就是坐在角门里河边树下，围观刘爷爷他们下棋，且一看便是一天。母亲杜巧兰起先还担忧这娃娃有什么毛病，想带他去找大夫看看。但刘爷爷他们却说，这孩子心静，将来指不定能成大事。毛天佑八岁那年，随母亲去南门大街赶集，在人群中与母亲走散了。但他不慌不忙，打量了一圈四周，在距离他最近的一个棋摊那坐了下来。下棋的大爷们起先不以为意。但在他们陷入僵局时，毛天佑小手一指，瞬间破局。等杜巧兰匆匆忙忙的找过来时，便见大爷们将毛天佑围在中间，啧啧称奇，问他师从何人。毛天佑则轻声的跟大爷们解释，称自己只是见多了别人下棋，跟着学会了一些。杜巧兰在那时开始意识到，她这个儿子，在棋艺上大概颇有天赋。
en: Mao Tianyou has always been a quiet child. Perhaps he inherits it from his reticent father, Mao Yi. While other boys his age dashed through the alleyways, shouting and chasing one another, Tianyou would appear in Forsaken Quarter, sitting silently beneath the old tree by the riverbank, watching Elderly Liu and the others play chess. Sometimes, he'd sit there the entire day. At first, his mother, Du Qiaolan, was worried. She feared something might be wrong with the boy and even considered taking him to a doctor. But Elderly Liu waved off her concerns, "That's not a problem. That's composure. He's got the makings of someone great." When Tianyou was eight, he followed his mother to the bustling market on South Gate Avenue. Amid the crowd's clamor, the two separated, but Tianyou didn't panic. He stood still, calmly scanned his surroundings, then walked to a chess stall and sat down. At first, the elderly men playing there paid him little attention. But as their game reached a deadlock, Tianyou quietly pointed at a piece and suggested a move that broke the stalemate. When Du Qiaolan anxiously rushed over and finally found him, she saw Tianyou was surrounded by elders. They were astonished, peppering him with questions: Who was his teacher? Tianyou calmly explained that he'd simply watched others play and figured a few things out on his own. That was the first time Du Qiaolan realized her son might be gifted in chess.

zh:
她最初的记忆，是一团火，一团迫近的火。
火触木，木坠；火触草，草熔；火触水，水沸……
若火触我身，我当何如？这便是她最初的问题。
随之而来的问题比火更快地挤满了她的思绪——何以火触万物，其色不一？其味不一？火有终乎？其终为何？我为火乎？我何为我？ 
打断她思绪的，是一声“姐姐，快跑！”
这便是她所闻的第一声呼唤。 
一双手比火更先触碰到她，带着她狂奔起来，火落于后，风行于侧，哭声不绝耳，苍穹出于前。
世间便在她最初的奔跑中缓缓生出。 
在漫无尽头的奔跑中，她逐渐明白，在前方拉着她的人，是她的“弟弟”。 
而她要很久很久后，才能明白，她所逃离的那团火，世人将如此描述：战火四起，野火焚村，杀人剪草，骨肉流离。 
失乡之人谈起野火，恨而泪下：都怪那日的火！是那场火毁了我们的家！是那场火杀了这么多的人。 
彼时她还不能顺畅的使用词句，只是自顾自吐出几个模仿来的音节：人。杀人。火。温暖。 
她的话如石投水般，激起更大的声浪——“傻子”、“天残”、“累赘”……“还不扔了了事！”
她并不能完全明白语义，但看懂了，众人憎恶她，如憎野火。 
“弟弟”又一次拉起她的手，朝众人喊了些什么。
再然后，“弟弟”拉着她，又走了很远很远的路，这一次，路有尽头，路的尽头，是一个人。
一个像鸟儿一样有着美丽羽毛的人。 鸟儿一样的人像“弟弟”一样，拉起她的另一只手，对他们说：走，回家去。 
她问：“你是谁？ ”
人说：“从今以后，我就是你们的母亲了！” 
她问：“那我是谁？”
人说：“你？哦——你们有名字吗？”
他们三人越过了一座很高的山，但这一次，路却很短，大抵因为归家的路，是有方向的。 
群山之后，“父亲”来迎他们。
“父亲”与“母亲”研究一夜后，告诉她：“你叫应宁，他叫应安。” 
从今日起，她有了父亲、母亲、弟弟，还有了名字。  
那么从今日起，她不再是一团野火，她确乎是个人了。  
可是，这个错误的推论，会在久远的以后向她索要代价。  
火收走了她谬误之论推导出的一切——“名字”、“父亲”、“母亲”、“弟弟”，甚至是“奔跑”。 
她将重新退还为火，但是，她隐隐觉得，这一次，不同。
她不会如野火一般，暴烈地吞噬一切。 
因为野火收走了能见到的一切，但他们留给她的东西如深埋在土地之下的种子，等待着从一颗心里爬出来，从眼睛里缓缓流下。
en:
Her earliest memory was fire, a mass of fire closing in.
When fire touched wood, wood fell. When it touched grass, grass shriveled. When it touched water, water boiled.

If fire touched me, what would become of me?
That was her first question.

And then came more questions, crowding into her mind even faster than the flames. Why did fire take on a different color with everything it touched, a different smell? Did fire have an end? And if it did, what lay at that end? Was she fire? What made her herself?
Then a voice broke through her thoughts.

"Sister, run!"
That was the first call she ever heard.

A pair of hands reached her before the fire did and pulled her into a run. The flames fell behind, the wind rushed at her side, cries filled her ears, and the sky opened ahead of her.
And in that first run, the world slowly began to take shape.

Somewhere in that endless flight, she came to understand that the one tugging her forward was her "younger brother."
It would be a very long time before she understood the words people used for the fire she had fled from: war spreading in every direction, wildfire burning villages, lives cut down like grass, families driven apart.
When those who had lost their homes spoke of that fire, they wept with hatred.

"It was that fire."
"That fire destroyed our home."
"That fire killed so many people."

At the time she still could not really speak. She only repeated a few sounds she had picked up for herself.

"People. Kill. Fire. Warmth."

Her words fell like stones into water and stirred up even louder voices.

"Idiot."
"Half-formed thing."
"Dead weight."
"Why not throw her away and be done with it?"

She could not fully understand the words, but she understood this much: they hated her, the way they hated wildfire.
Her "younger brother" took her hand again and shouted something back at them.

After that he led her a very, very long way. But this time the road had an end, and at the end of it stood a person.
A person with beautiful feathers, like a bird.

Like her "younger brother," that bird-like person took her other hand and said to them, "Come on. Let's go home."
She asked, "Who are you?"
The person said, "From today on, I am your mother."
She asked, "Then who am I?"
The person said, "You? Oh... do you have names?"

The three of them crossed a very high mountain. But this time the road felt short. Perhaps the road home always does, once it has a direction.
Beyond the mountains, "father" came to meet them.
After father and mother spent the whole night discussing it, they told her, "Your name is Ying Ning. His is Ying An."

From that day on, she had a father, a mother, a younger brother, and a name.
From that day on, she was no longer just a piece of wildfire. She was truly a person.

But that mistaken conclusion would one day come back to demand its price.
Fire took back everything that conclusion had given her: her "name," her "father," her "mother," her "younger brother," even her "running."
She would be given back to fire once more.

And yet, dimly, she felt that this time it would be different.
She would not be like wildfire, raging out and devouring everything in sight.

Wildfire had taken everything she could see. But what they had left her was like a seed buried deep in the earth, waiting to climb out of a heart and slowly fall from the eyes.

zh:
兔子衔草，吉祥报福。

兔子因其繁殖能力强盛，被视为多子多福的象征。宋代民间有兔子音同吐子的说法，故而瓷器描绘，常出现‘兔子纹’用来表示多子多福。兔子纹样所用甚多，北宋时期‘刘家功夫针铺’的白兔儿铜版，是中国最早的商标标记。
en:
A rabbit with a sprig of grass foretells joy and blessings. 

Rabbits were seen as symbols of fertility and abundance due to their prolific breeding. Among the Song populace, the word for "rabbit" (tu) was considered a homonym for "spitting out children" (tu zi), so porcelain often featured rabbit motifs to symbolize fertility. Rabbit patterns were widely used. One of China's earliest known trademarks was a copperplate design of a white rabbit for the "Liu Family's Kung Fu Needle Shop" in the Northern Song period.

汪汪，汪！汪汪汪，汪汪汪汪汪汪汪汪汪？汪汪！汪汪汪汪汪汪。

……

少东家：

哥又来同你叨叨乐子啦！

这一趟出游，哥算是涨了见识，刚一进开封城，就叫一看门的狗给拦住了。那狗三催四请，非要哥去什么皇城脚下，听什么“汪汪队唠嗑年终总结大会”。别的不说，现场狗粮管够，还热闹得紧。

光是逛了一小会儿，哥就听了不少壁角。

什么下属暗恋头儿啊，什么宫里头的官爷今天穿了身什么私服啦……嗐，听得哥那是嘴角就没下来过！

哦对了，哥还在现场遇见个跟我撞脸的大黄狗，竟也叫伏禄娃的名儿。

那伏禄二娃虚荣得紧，逢狗就吹自己跟了个名声响的游侠，好像是叫什么、什么$C$L#Y$PN#E$C的……哥没听过，也不在乎！

出门在外，身份是自个儿给的，哥当即将你的家业同人品，夸得那是天花乱坠，杀得对面那是无地自容。

那伏禄小二娃竟还敢同哥犟嘴，张口就是“我们少东家会捡别人擦屁股用的小树杈，你们会吗？我们少东家杀人又抢马，往人家屁股蛋子上射完箭还能跑掉，你们能吗？我们少东家一年能整八次容，你们能吗？”

听得哥那是一愣一愣！

不过，少东家你放心，输狗不输阵，靠着哥这口亮嗓门，到底没落了你的面子！

好了不多说了，前头那台上突然站了个狗模狗样的汪，瞧那架势，是要发号施令了，你等哥回去后再同你细唠。

你最靠谱的伏禄娃留
en:
Woof, woof! Woof? Woof woof! Woof.
...
Young Master:
I'm back to bark about more fun stuff!
I've really seen it all on this trip. As soon as I entered Kaifeng City, I was stopped by a dog guarding the gate. That dog was so insistent, practically begging me to go to the base of the Imperial walls for some "Barking Brigade Year-End Summary Meeting." If nothing else, there was plenty of dog food, and it was quite lively.
Just from wandering around a bit, I overheard a lot of gossip.
Subordinates crushing on their bosses, what kind of casual clothes the palace officials are wearing today... Hah, I couldn't stop grinning!
Oh, right, I also met a big yellow dog there who looks just like me. He actually goes by the name Fu Luwa, too.
That Fulu Erwa is incredibly vain. He brags to every dog he meets about his famous wanderer master, someone called $C$L#Y$PN#E$C or something... I've never heard of them, and I don't care!
When you're out and about, you give yourself your own status. I immediately started praising your Homestead and your character to high heaven, making the other guy feel utterly ashamed.
That Fulu Erwa actually dared to talk back to me! He barked, "Our Young Master can pick up twigs used as primitive toilet paper, can yours? Our Young Master kills people and steals horses, and can outrun anyone after shooting arrows into their butts, can yours? Our Young Master can change his face eight times a year, can yours?"
I was absolutely stunned!
But don't worry, Young Master, I didn't back down. With my loud barking, I definitely didn't let you lose face!
Anyway, I'll stop here. Some dog-faced guy just stood up on the stage over there, looking like he's about to give orders. I'll tell you more when I get back.
Your most reliable Fu Luwa

zh:
醉花阴原不过是金陵城中的一间歌舞花坊，因与徐知诰的姻亲而发迹，却也因此而成为亲贵间秘而不宣的笑料。
直至天祐十五年广陵事发，徐知诰闻风起事，一夜诛尽叛逆，底定南国政权。有人事后细细察探，只觉巧合背后盘丝错节，必有人斡旋连横、穿针引线，而线头竟直指醉花阴。
有心人大惊之余，方觉过往之泥潭残蕊、亲贵笑料，竟已一跃九霄，凡俗难攀。无数达官贵客沉醉花间，千金买笑；而花团锦簇背后的盘根错节，则悄然隐于十丈软红间。
en:
The Velvet Shade was originally just one tavern in the city, started by a relative of Xu Zhihao. This was actually an unspoken joke between the nobles. 
It was not until the fifteenth year of the Tianyou Era when Xu Zhihao took action, killing the traitors overnight and solidifying his grip on power. Some people looked into this afterward, and pieced the puzzle together. It was one coincidence after another, as if someone was guiding them. Eventually, the clues pointed to the Velvet Shade. 
They were stunned at first, but soon realized that the butt of the joke in the past has soared beyond their reach. Countless nobles and officials were now lost among the blossoms, buying joy with gold. The tangled web of power hid behind the dazzling splendor of flowers, veiled by the softness of the crimson world.

风角术，为中国古代的一种古老术数。

风是阴阳二气的产物，有人以此推论，神灵作为强大的存在，可以用自己的能力来改变阴阳均衡的局面，因此大风天气的出现，或预兆着神灵降临。
en:
Wind divination is an ancient Chinese form of omen reading. Practitioners observed the wind's direction, strength, speed, its color and other visible signs, and the time it rose, to predict good or ill fortune.

In classical cosmology, wind is born of the interplay of yin and yang. Some reasoned that powerful spirits could disrupt that balance, so the arrival of fierce winds might be taken as an omen of a divine presence.

zh:
杯酒释兵权后，武臣势微，文士得势。此后局势如何，坊间多有议论。然予观之，世事如棋，皆在贵人局中，天下大势，已见端倪。
外传石守信武库藏兵，为赵大忌。然则武库之兵，暗流鬼市，或皆贵人暗操。于贵人而言，国库充盈；于石将军而言，后人得保。两相裨益，何乐不为？（老山注：孙海那小子交代了，让老夫替他标个重点。此段重点是……去武庙看看就知道了！）

普公遇刺之事，众口皆认军器监与引见司有嫌。然凭其力，恐不能成。寿昌坊内，暗流涌动，人心叵测，尤以金街四少为甚。纨绔之名是假，借名行事，恐才是真。（老山注：金街四少，不简单！）

人皆道鬼市诡谲，殊不知地上开封，亦非净土。吾今冒昧论此局势，是为警示后来之人，慎入是非之地，以免祸及己身。（老山注：总之，快去蹚浑水吧！）
en:
After the emperor's banquet where military power was stripped from the generals, the warriors declined and the scholars rose. People gossip about what comes next, but mark my words: this is all part of the game played by those in high places. The tides have already turned. They say Shi Shouxin's secret armory was a thorn in the emperor's side. Yet those weapons, now flowing through the Ghostlight Market, are likely controlled by the very elites the emperor once trusted. A win-win: the court gets its coffers filled, General Shi secures his legacy. (Laoshan's note: Sun Hai insisted I highlight this... Want the real answer? Go visit the Martial Temple!)

As for Minister Pu's assassination, everyone blames the Armaments Bureau and the Imperial Audiences Office, but those small fries couldn't pull it off. Prosperity Haven's undercurrents run deep, especially around the "Goldwater Four." Their playboy act is just a cover. (Laoshan's note: Don't underestimate those people!)

People call the Ghostlight Market treacherous, but above ground? Kaifeng's no paradise. I write this as a warning: tread carefully, lest you drown in the chaos. (Laoshan's note: Or better yet, go stir the pot!)

北去滹沱的路途艰辛，他见难民遍地，遇逃兵争斗，遭山匪要挟。

唯独那块师弟们赠予的无事牌，他还好好藏在身边。

只是千里奔赴的遥途，令玉牌也在无意间磕碎了一角。
他有些懊恼自己的不小心，想着等往后闲暇无事时再补好。
他重整衣冠，继续往前，

en:
Brant never imagined that one day he would travel so far. The road north to Hutuo was a hard one. Along the way he saw refugees scattered everywhere, deserters fighting among themselves, and bandits lying in wait. His hair fell into disarray, his green robe was soaked through, and even his pack was lost. Only the jade token his junior brothers had given him remained safely tucked away at his side.
Yet over the course of that thousand-mile journey, even the token was chipped at one corner. He was annoyed with himself for being so careless and thought he would mend it when he had the time. So he straightened his clothes and pressed on, toward another broken corner beyond the mountain, one ravaged by war. That patch of the world, too, was waiting for him to make it whole.

【襄公第九】

元年，春，王正月，公即位。
继正即立，正也。

系彭城于宋者，不与鱼石，正也。
○夏，晋韩厥帅师伐郑。仲孙蔑会齐崔杼、曹人、邾人、杞人次于鄫。
○秋，楚公子壬夫帅师侵宋。
○九月，辛酉，天王崩。
○邾子来朝。
○冬，卫侯使公孙剽来聘。晋侯使荀罃来聘。

二年，春，王正月，葬简王。
○郑师伐宋。
○夏，五月，庚寅，夫人姜氏薨。
○六月，庚辰，郑伯睔卒。
○晋师、宋师、卫宁殖侵郑。
其曰卫宁殖，如是而称于前事也。
○秋，七月，仲孙蔑会晋荀罃、宋华元、卫孙林父、曹人、邾人于戚。
○己丑，葬我小君齐姜。
○叔孙豹如宋。
○冬，仲孙蔑会晋荀罃、齐崔杼、宋华元、卫孙林父、曹人、邾人、滕人、薛人、小邾人于戚，城于虎牢。
若言中国焉，内郑也。
○楚杀其大夫公子申。

……
en:
【Duke Xiang, Ninth Year】

First year, spring, the king's first month, the duke assumed the throne.
Succeeding the rightful ruler and ascending to the throne is proper.
○Zhongsun Mie met with Jin Luan Yan, Song Hua Yuan, Wei Ning Zhi, Cao people, Ju people, Zhu people, Teng people, and Xue people to besiege Song's Pengcheng.
Attributing Pengcheng to Song is to refuse Yu Shi, which is proper.
○Summer, Jin Han Jue led troops to attack Zheng. Zhongsun Mie met with Qi Cui Zhu, Cao people, Zhu people, and Qi people and stationed at Zeng.
○Autumn, Chu's prince Ren Fu led troops to invade Song.
○September, Xinyou, the king of Heaven passed away.
○The Viscount of Zhu came for an audience.
○Winter, the Marquis of Wei sent Gongsun Piao to pay a visit. The Marquis of Jin sent Xun Ying to pay a visit.

Second year, spring, the king's first month, King Jian was buried.
○Zheng's troops attacked Song.
○Summer, fifth month, Gengyin, Lady Jiang passed away.
○Sixth month, Gengchen, Earl Kun of Zheng died.
○Jin's troops, Song's troops, and Wei Ning Zhi invaded Zheng.
Calling him Wei Ning Zhi is to commend him for his previous deeds.
○Autumn, seventh month, Zhongsun Mie met with Jin Xun Ying, Song Hua Yuan, Wei Sun Lin Fu, Cao people, and Zhu people at Qi.
○Jichou, our minor ruler Qi Jiang was buried.
○Shu Sun Bao went to Song.
○Winter, Zhongsun Mie met with Jin Xun Ying, Qi Cui Zhu, Song Hua Yuan, Wei Sun Lin Fu, Cao people, Zhu people, Teng people, Xue people, and minor Zhu people at Qi, and built a city at Hulao.
Speaking of it as within the Central States is to treat Zheng as internal.
○Chu killed its high official Prince Shen.

All visiting emissaries were lodged here, and state documents, maps, and regional tributes were all stored within its walls. en:
The Jade of Way once belonged to Murong Yuan's mother, Chu Yun, a former disciple of the Mohist School. 
In the chaos of war, a young girl lost everything. Clutching the wooden eagle her mother had crafted, she clung to life by a thread. With help from a kind soul, she learned to survive in the world. 
But the world is cruel. The one who once shielded her from the northern snows would eventually entrust her to someone else on another snowy night. Confused and hurt, she buried her doubts and turned her heart fully to the path of tool and craft. 
With talent and relentless study, Murong Yuan restored the very wooden eagle that once carried her to safety. 
In her pursuit of mastery, she scoured the land. 
When she learned that the Jade of Way she carried was an antique of the Mohist School, she realized she had found her path forward. 
She believed that one day, her flying eagle would soar in the sky and never fall again.

竹骨篇

系线术 
长鸢三线，短鹞独绳。线车需檀木作轴，引绳以柘蚕丝为芯，外缠野麻护损。打结处缀响弓，破空作鸾哨。  
试飞谱
北地放鸢，择清明后南风初起；江南试鹞，待重九前新露未晞。初飞系石三十步，次第减之，若负羽行沙，方得逍遥。
en:
Bamboo Frame Chapter:
Take three sections of bamboo: the root section for the body, stiff and unyielding against the wind; the middle section shaved for the wings, flexible to store momentum; the tip section for the tail, fine as a fishing line. Bend it by roasting over a fire, but do not let it turn charred and brittle.
Pasting Formula:
Soak plain, single-thread silk in light glue, stretching it over the frame as taut as a drum. Reinforce the seams secretly with ramie, a technique known as the "Iron Net Locking the Clouds." In summer, switch to mulberry paper, mixing the paste with Sichuan peppercorns to ward off silverfish.
Coloring Chapter:
For the blue sky color, mix Buddha's head indigo with alum; for the crimson twilight, boil sappanwood for its juice. When painting birds of prey, dot the eyes with pine soot; when depicting cranes, dip the feet in gold paste. Once the colors dry, scatter fine porcelain powder over them so they glitter in the sunlight.
Tethering Technique:
Use three lines for a long kite, and a single cord for a short sparrow-hawk kite. The spool must be made of sandalwood. The core of the tether should be wild silk, wrapped in wild hemp to prevent wear. Tie a sounding bow at the knot, so it cuts through the air with a phoenix's whistle.
Flight Manual:
To fly a kite in the North, wait for the first southern winds after the Qingming Festival; to test a kite in Jiangnan, wait for the fresh dew to dry before the Double Ninth Festival. For its maiden flight, tie a stone at thirty paces, and gradually reduce the weight. Only when it glides like a feather drifting over sand can it achieve true freedom.

扉页标注：
我门弟子避世而非忘世，藏踪行遍四海，以机关暗助苍生。
千虑有失，难免无意暴露墨门身份。诸同门可以此书为戒，反思举止破绽。

第一计·引蛇出洞

在这个纷繁复杂的江湖里，存在着一类特殊人群——墨山道。
和堂堂正正的九流门不一样，墨山道的门规奇奇怪怪，在外游历的弟子，都得把本事藏严实了。

老话说得好，只要是演的，那就一定是假的！
和那些唱唱跳跳的门派、酒蒙子门派不一样啊，九流门的能人，在人群中这么一扫，就能认出谁是墨山道来。

常见墨山道弟子分为两类：一类是明目张胆的显性，一类是深藏不露的隐性。
不论是哪种，他们都有个共同点：见到机关后神情古怪，眼神游移。

如果你问孤云：这题能算出来，算你厉害。他们就会奋不顾身奔向题海。
而墨山道的弟子，要么盯着机关若有所思，要么看见工造斜眼观瞧。此时你拿出一件机关小物大喊：拆得出来，算你厉害！
——墨山弟子十有八九无法抗拒这样的诱惑。

至于认出以后，是真情实感找他们帮忙做做机关，还是见义勇为拆穿伪装，那就各凭心意了。

更多高端辨识技巧，请凭书签前往鬼市古书铺，回复“续阅”，更多精彩等你来！
en:
Title Page:
Our disciples steer clear of the world but don't forget it. They travel far and wide in secret, using mechanisms to quietly help others.
No matter how careful you are, slips happen, and sometimes a disciple's identity is accidentally revealed. Let this book serve as a warning to reflect on your actions and avoid such mistakes.

Strategy One: Lure Them Out

Unlike the Nine Mortal Ways, Mohist Hill has odd rules, and their disciples must keep their skills tightly under wraps in the jianghu.
As the old saying goes: if they're putting on an act, it's bound to be a sham!
Unlike those sects of dancing peacocks or bumbling drunks, the skilled folks of the Nine Mortal Ways can spot a Mohist Hill disciple from a crowd. Mohist Hill disciples come in two types: the overt and the covert. But both share one thing in common: when they see a mechanism, their expressions change, and their eyes dart nervously.
Tell a Lone Cloud disciple, "I'll call you a genius if you solve this," and they'll dive right in. Mohist Hill disciples, however, either stare thoughtfully or scrutinize mechanisms from the corner of their eyes. Most Mohist Hill disciples can't resist the challenge of dismantling mechanical gadgets. Once they reveal themselves, it's up to you to decide whether to ask them for help or to see through their disguise.

For more advanced tips, visit the Antique Bookshop with the bookmark and reply "Continue Reading." More exciting secrets await!

zh:
没有、没有，还是没有。
佛手郎卸下所有气力，拽着手边的绳索坐在雪地里。

不是说叔父年轻时便是在大散关得的东西，放进了匣子里么？它的钥匙应当在此处才对。
可佛手郎用量绳的尖头在崖壁上刻了好多道记录的纹路，仍是一无所获。

生了火，佛手郎少见地怪罪起叔父来。
一个上了世间最好的锁的匣子，它的继承人却不知如何打开。
篝火暖融融的，佛手郎的眼前朦朦胧胧现出一个影子。影子夺过他手里的绳索，嗖一声把它丢到大散关的那头，哗啦一下把高高的崖壁拉倒了。

大散关倒了，所有人都可以过关去！
影子忘情地呐喊，佛手郎却注意到他的头顶被一块巨大山石的阴影覆盖了。来不及思考，佛手郎便朝着影子扑了过去——

就这样，佛手郎扑到了雪地里。他抬起头，发现风雪变大，手边的绳索早已不知所踪。
回去吧、回去吧。
没有这定胜的宝物，我佛手郎一样可以护住凉州，一样可以带所有人过关。
叔父，你也是这么想的吧？
en:
Nothing, nothing, still nothing. 
Exhausted, Buddha-Hand Lad grabs a rope and sits in the snow. 

Wasn't it said that his uncle obtained something at Dasan Pass in his youth and placed it in a box? The key should be here. 
But after carving many marks on the cliff with the measuring rope's tip, he finds nothing. 

By the fire, Buddha-Hand Lad rarely blames his uncle: 
A box locked with the world's finest lock, yet its heir doesn't know how to open it. 
Warm firelight blurs his vision—a shadow appears. It snatches the rope from him, flings it beyond Dasan Pass, and with a crash, pulls down the high cliff. 

Dasan Pass has fallen! Now everyone can pass through! 
The shadow cheers wildly, but Buddha-Hand Lad notices a huge rock looming above its head. Without thinking, he lunges at the shadow— 

And landed facedown in snow. He looks up; the storm has worsened, the rope gone. 
Go back, go back. 
Even without this treasure, I, Buddha-Hand Lad, can protect Liangzhou. I can take everyone through. 
Uncle, you thought so too, didn't you?

zh:
“夜耿耿而不寐兮，魂憧憧而至曙。风骚骚而四起兮，霜皑皑而依庭……”
漏三下，禁中冷宫，废苑枯井，幽咽乍起。井旁枯槐，无风自动，倏垂白绫三尺。
恍惚间，见一倒悬素影，发覆其面，不见其容，似吟离思之赋。其声如诉，其字如血，次第生于白绫之上……
若试窥之，目光即为之所引，魂为其所夺，魄为其所摄。
故传，此乃诗魂索句成赋也。
en:
"O, wakeful I lie through the long night; my restless soul flutters until the dawn. The winds sough and sigh on every side; white frost clings to the courtyard..."
At the third watch, deep within the Forlorn Palace, a faint, mournful sobbing arises from a dry well in a ruined garden. Beside the well, a withered locust tree stirs without a breeze, and a three-foot length of white silk suddenly unfurls.
In a trance, one sees an inverted pale shadow, hair veiling its face, seemingly chanting a rhapsody of parting sorrows. Its voice is full of sorrow, and each word, as it is spoken, blooms one by one across the white silk in strokes red as blood...
Should one dare a glimpse, the gaze is drawn, the soul ensnared, and the spirit seized.
Thus it is said: this is a Poet's Soul, seeking verses to weave into a rhapsody.

zh:
加入玄元教之前，邓一灯也算个小人物。
有一身稍高的武功，一嘴不逊的口才，足够他在什么地方混得不错。
邓一灯听说玄元教中皆能人。有什么人能比我还能？他这么想着，就动身去玄元教驻地一探。才蹲在山头上的竹子上看了一眼，玄元教徒的罡风就把他脚底的竹林削剩他站着那根。
好家伙！邓一灯落荒而逃。
玄元教、玄元教。邓一灯念着这个名字练功，从日出练到日落，从黑夜练到白天，就为了亲自进入玄元教，看看里头到底有什么能人异士。
邓一灯如愿加入了玄元教。在江湖之上，他多少能出点风头；可入了玄元教，他的能耐却只够看大门。
这门，他看得兴趣寥寥，日日伸长了脖子往内院看。
正看得出神，一块石子精准地弹到邓一灯的脑瓜仁上。恰到好处地疼，又完全没伤到他。
邓一灯抬眼望去。
“嘿，兄弟，整几块石子玩玩？”
en:
Before he ever set foot in the Xuanyuan Cult, Deng Yideng was already someone of note.
His martial skills were solid, and his mouth even sharper. With those two alone, he could get by just fine wherever Jianghu took him.
He'd heard that the Xuanyuan Cult was full of true masters. How good could they really be? Better than me? Curious, nd a little smug, he set off to see for himself. He'd barely crouched atop a bamboo stalk on the hillside when a blast of Astral Wind from the cultists sliced the entire bamboo grove clean off. Every stalk but the one he stood on.
"Holy hell!"Deng Yideng scrambled away in a panic.
Xuanyuan Cult... From that day on, he repeated the name as he trained, from sunrise to sunset, night into dawn, driven by the thought that one day, he'd walk through those gates openly, and see just how many extraordinary people were hidden inside.
Eventually, he did get in. Out in the Jianghu, Deng Yideng could still make a name for himself. Inside the Xuanyuan Cult, though, his skills were only enough to earn him gate duty.
He did the job halfheartedly, craning his neck all day to peer toward the inner grounds.
Lost in thought, a pebble pinged precisely off the center of his forehead. The throw was precise: it hurt just enough to sting, without leaving a mark.
He looked up.
"Yo, brother. Up for skipping a few stones?"

zh:
波陈人来得太快，打断了那个连通整个河西的计划。
将军让我走，毕竟胡杨集不同关隘，是守不住的。
但我不想走，这里是我的故乡。
僵持之下，我便和他说：想让我走，除非你拿最珍视的东西来换。
困守安西的将军，还能剩下什么珍贵之物呢？可他偏偏从怀里掏出一本册子，那是一本抚恤金的花名册。
我很清楚的知道这本花名册上，名字的含义。
那些名字，很多我都见过。
我们曾一起筑井，一起建设胡杨集。
只是一转眼，那些人就变成了花名册上冷冰冰的墨字。
我知道他一直想把这份名单，带回长安。
“好事都让你做了，你在乎长安，在乎这里，在乎每一个将士、乡民，那你呢？”
“我，也交给你了。”
我这才看到花名册末尾的两个字。
他的名字。
en:
The Bodchen came too fast, shattering the plan to connect all of Hexi.
The general urged me to leave. Poplar Bazaar was not a fortress; it could not be held.
But I would not go. This is my home.
At our impasse, I challenged him: "If you want me to leave, trade me for what you treasure most."

What precious thing could a general trapped in Anxi possibly possess? Yet he reached into his tunic and pulled out a small ledger. It was a roster for the fallen, listing their condolence payments.
I knew precisely what those names meant.
I had known so many of them.
We had built the wells together. We had built Poplar Bazaar together.
In the blink of an eye, they had become cold, black ink on a page.
I knew he had always dreamt of carrying that list back to Chang'an himself.

"You carry the burden for everyone," I cried out. "For Chang'an, for this land, for every soldier. But what about you?"
"My fate," he said, "is in your hands now too."
And then I saw it. The final entry.
It was his own name.

Divinecraft heard that outside, people named their dogs and cats things like "Lucky" or "Fortune" or "Coin." How ordinary! How utterly common! Nothing like the name his owner had given him, Divinecraft, meaning "Heavenly Craftsmanship," evokes the wonders of creation and the ingenuity of inventors. What a wonderfully refined name!
Until one day, a Mohist Hill disciple visited the house. When he heard the cat's name, he burst out laughing. "Divinecraft? Hahaha! You must really, really want your diagrams to be collected by the Divinecraft Pavilion! Divinecraft. Ha!"
His owner protested, "What's so funny? It's like naming a dog 'Lucky'! It's just expressing a wish!"

走入万古一人殿的那一刻，朱鱼才知晓了神明的意义：有人活成神，是为了攀至众人之上，“河伯”们却更贪心，要以人之姿，试试与天争命。禹、李冰、王景……人有了无惧苍天的胆魄，便才有资格，成这万古一人的“河伯”。

这世上成败向来公平，有成，便有败，有失，便有得。若真有神话“四渎”中的龙，此地龙王……怕是全天下活得最憋屈的一位。朱鱼往后瞧了瞧仅剩的一尾“龙王”，抛去了丹丸，此药虽非有脱胎换骨之能，可若能缓解几分苦痛，又如何没有必要。按张彦卿的法子，不多久，龙王便认了主。按说书人所言：那许久不见的“河伯”竟在契丹北撤时驭龙而出，持剑敕令，叫这涛涛浊流化为九天水龙，东衔艨艟，西破舢船，叫那千万契丹兵士葬身浊涛，万劫不复！

“哪儿有那么夸张，都怪你长得怪，吓到了人家。”朱鱼笑着拍拍龙王的头，又扔出一瓶丹丸，龙王不满地“嘟囔”了两声，拨动鱼鳍，向朱鱼溅去几朵小水花，潜入水底，再不想理睬主人偶尔的调皮。
en:
It wasn't until she stepped into the Eternal Solitude Hall that Zhu Yu truly understood the meaning of divinity. Some ascend to godhood to stand above all others. But the "River Masters" were greedier still. They sought, while still mortal, to fight fate itself from the heavens. Yu the Great, Li Bing, Wang Jing... Only those who dared defy the sky itself were worthy to become River Masters, the eternal sovereigns of water.

In this world, victory and defeat are always fair. Where there is triumph, there must also be failure; where something is lost, something else is gained. If the Dragon Kings of the Four Rivers' myths truly existed, then the Dragon King of this place must surely be the most wretched of them all. Zhu Yu glanced back at the "Dragon King" who only had one tail left. She tossed over a bottle of elixirs. It wasn't a panacea, but if it could ease a little of the dragon king's suffering, was that not reason enough? Following Zhang Yanqing's method, it wasn't long before the Dragon King recognized her as master.

The Storyteller speaks: the long-gone River Master reappeared during the Khitan retreat. He rode a dragon into battle, wielding his sword to command the waters. The muddy torrents rose into nine heavenly dragons, devouring warships to the east, shattering boats to the west, and drowning tens of thousands of Khitan soldiers, dragging them into oblivion!

"It wasn't nearly that dramatic," Zhu Yu chuckled, patting the Dragon King's head. 

"You just looked so strange you scared them off." She tossed another bottle of elixirs.

The Dragon King grumbled in protest, flicked its fin to splash a few drops of water at her, then dove back beneath the surface, no longer willing to entertain the humor of its mischievous master.

zh:
绔绔是文津馆一带最不安分的猫，通体洁白，鼻尖一抹黑，像刚钻过灶膛。
它最大的乐趣是捉弄文津馆弟子。摊开的书页，踩上去印两朵梅花；搁在阶上的笔，拨到地上看人去捡。
唯独赵双双不吃这套。
赵双双性子急，脾气大，读不顺的书敢摔，辩不赢的理要追出去三里地。头一回撞见绔绔捣乱，她一把揪住它后颈皮，提到半空：“小东西，旁人的书怎能乱踩？你可识字？”
绔绔四脚乱蹬，冲她哈气。
赵双双也冲它哈了一口气。
绔绔愣住了。它这辈子没被人凶过。
自此，绔绔专挑赵双双在的时候生事：将她誊好的纸页拖下案来，在她的砚台里涮尾巴尖。赵双双撵着绔绔从东到西，可真追上了，却只是把它抱在怀里一通揉搓，嘴里骂着“泼皮赖猫”，指间却轻得像拈一片羽毛。
近来赵双双被罚清扫前庭，扫帚抡得呼呼生风。绔绔偏挑这时候来，先扑那扫拢的落叶堆，又伸爪去拨她手中扫帚的竿尖。
这次赵双双没有撵它，只是看了它好一会儿，忽然蹲下身，把猫捞起来摁在肩上。
“笨猫。”她声音闷闷的，“那是罚扫，你当是玩儿呢。”
那天路过的弟子看见，赵双双一手抱着猫，一手握着扫帚，辩经堂被扫得干干净净。绔绔趴在她肩头，尾巴垂下来，随着扫帚悠悠地晃。
en:
Dandy is the most unruly cat around the Inkbound Order, pure white from head to tail except for a smudge of black on the tip of its nose, as though it had just poked into a kitchen stove. Its greatest joy is tormenting the disciples: treading across open books to leave plum-blossom paw prints, or knocking brushes off steps just to watch people scramble to retrieve them.
Only Zhao Shuangshuang refused to put up with it. Shuangshuang had a fiery temper and little patience, ready to fling aside any text that baffled her and chase an opponent for miles over an unresolved dispute. The first time she caught Dandy making mischief, she hoisted the cat into the air by the scruff of its neck. "You little wretch, how dare you trample on someone else's books? Can you even read?"
Dandy kicked its paws wildly and hissed. Shuangshuang hissed right back. Dandy froze; never in its life had anyone dared cross it.
From that day on, Dandy deliberately sought trouble whenever Shuangshuang was around, dragging her freshly transcribed sheets off the desk and dipping the tip of its tail into her inkstone. Shuangshuang would chase Dandy from one end of the hall to the other, but once she caught it, she would only bundle the cat into her arms for a good knead, scolding it as a "worthless rogue cat" while her fingers brushed as softly as down.
Recently, Shuangshuang was assigned to sweep the front courtyard as punishment, her broom sweeping with brisk whooshes. Dandy picked this exact moment to cause trouble, first pouncing into the freshly swept pile of leaves, then pawing at the tip of her broom.
This time Shuangshuang did not chase it. She watched the cat for a long time before suddenly crouching down, lifting it up, and resting it on her shoulder. "Foolish cat," she murmured softly, "this is punishment sweeping. You think it's a game?"
Disciples passing by that day saw Shuangshuang holding the cat in one arm and the broom in the other, having swept the Debating Hall spotless. Dandy lay draped over her shoulder, tail dangling and swaying gently with the rhythm of the broom.

其一为“望安西”。望安屯地处要冲，可遥望玉门关。常日有屯田将士于屯北铸币厂塔楼值守，东望玉门关。晨角暮鼓，以传消息。玉门关灯火长明，望安屯炊烟袅袅，相望不离。
其二为“望平安”。望安屯纳地方百姓，凡无可去者，皆可于望安屯落脚。昔年望安屯军民一体，家家夜不闭户路不拾遗。
其三之意，村民未言明。只云昔年唐廷宣诏，群情雀跃，军民静候王师东来。然王师未至，沙暴袭来，屯中兵民四散，屋垣塌毁。今空留几户人家，尚有人烟。昔年盛景，终难再现。
en:
Peaceward Camp was first built during the Dali period, originally serving as a reclamation and coin-casting site for the Anxi Army. Located beside Jade Gate Pass, it slopes from north to south. According to the surviving villagers, Peaceward carries three meanings.
Firstly, "looking toward Anxi." As a strategic hub, Peaceward Camp overlooks Jade Gate Pass. Garrison soldiers stationed at the tower of the coin-casting factory north of the camp would gaze east at Jade Gate Pass daily. Bugles at dawn and drums at dusk relayed messages. The lights of Jade Gate Pass burned bright, and the cooking smoke of Peaceward Camp curled upward. They watched over each other, never apart.
Secondly, "looking forward to peace." Peaceward Camp sheltered local people, whoever had nowhere to go could settle here. In the past, soldiers and civilians in Peaceward Camp lived as one, with doors left unlocked at night and lost belongings untouched on the roads.
The third meaning was left unspoken by the villagers. They only said that in the past, when the Tang court issued an imperial edict, the people rejoiced, and soldiers and civilians waited quietly for the imperial army to arrive from the east. Yet the army never came, instead, a sandstorm struck, scattering the soldiers and civilians, and collapsing the houses. Today, only a few households remain, clinging to life. The prosperity of the past can never be restored.

萧鹤衣带着两柄剑，和他的朋友一起出门游历。

这一路，他们曾在闹市中一掷千金，拍下罪人之物，被人追杀。
也曾身无分文，一起蹲在他乡的巷角乞讨。
他们曾爬上华山的凌寒绝顶，见过传说中的三道剑意。
也曾在云梦泽的水阵差点溺死，衣衫尽湿，被苗女捉弄嘲笑。
但第二柄剑从未出鞘。

直到中渡桥战败，混乱来临。
林险生狼狈地逃出。杜重威、契丹、神秘的帐中人。他们一个都没“打过”。
当契丹兵乘胜袭来，流民身前只有他们俩，萧鹤衣抛出了那柄剑，打醒他的朋友。

那是儿时互换的礼物。赠君宝剑，与君同行。
我承诺，你还站着，我就不会倒下。
离家、闯江湖，上前线。无论何事，我都奉陪。
随后剑光如太极生生不息，以两人之剑，退一军之敌。
新的剑阵诞生，很多人的命得以保全。
后来江湖说，幸甚，一双新秀。
en:
Xiao Heyi set out to travel with two swords and his friends.

Along the way, they squandered fortunes in bustling markets to bid on a sinner's belongings and were hunted for it.
They also found themselves penniless, huddling in the corners of foreign alleys to beg.
They climbed the frigid peaks of Mount Hua and witnessed the legendary three sword intents.
They nearly drowned in the water formations of Dreamy Marsh, soaked to the bone and mocked by the local girls.
But the second sword never left its sheath.

Until the defeat at Zhongdu Bridge, when chaos descended.
Lin Xiansheng fled in a wretched state. Du Chongwei, the Khitans, the mysterious figure in the tent—they "defeated" none of them.
As the Khitan soldiers struck in their moment of victory and the refugees stood defenseless, Xiao Heyi threw that sword to wake his friend.

It was a gift they had exchanged as children. A precious blade for a friend, to walk the path together.
"I promise: as long as you stand, I will not fall."
"Leaving home, roaming the world, heading to the front—no matter the task, I am with you."
Then, sword light surged like the endless cycle of Tai Chi; with two blades, they repelled an entire army.
A new sword formation was born, and many lives were saved.
Later, the world of martial arts would say: "What luck to have such a pair of rising stars."
Waaah... Mom... I'm scared...
Come on in for a drink, won't ya? It's warmer that way.

zh:
【士昏礼第二】

昏礼。下达，纳采，用雁。主人筵于户西，西上，右几。使者玄端至。摈者出请事，入告。主人如宾服，迎于门外，再拜。宾不答拜。揖入。至于庙门，揖入。三揖，至于阶，三让。主人以宾升，西面。宾升西阶，当阿，东面致命。主人阼阶上，北面再拜。授于楹间，南面。宾降，出。主人降，授老雁。
摈者出请宾执雁，请问名。主人许。宾入，授如初礼。
摈者出请宾告事毕，入告，出请醴宾。宾礼辞，许。主人彻几改筵，东上，侧尊甒醴于房中。主人迎宾于庙门外，揖让如初，升。主人北面再拜。宾西阶上，北面答拜。主人拂几授校，拜送。宾以几辟，北面，设于坐左之西阶上，答拜。赞者酌醴，加角柶面叶，出于房。主人受醴，面枋，筵前西北面。宾拜受醴，复位。主人阼阶上拜送。赞者荐脯醢。宾即筵坐，左执觯，祭脯醢，以柶祭醴三，西阶上北面坐，啐醴，建柶，兴，坐奠觯，遂拜。主人答拜。宾即筵，奠于荐左，降筵，北面坐取脯。主人辞。宾降，授人脯，出。主人送于门外，再拜。
纳吉，用雁，如纳采礼。
纳征，玄𫄸束帛、俪皮，如纳吉礼。
请期，用雁。主人辞，宾许，告期，如纳征礼。
期，初昏，陈三鼎于寝门外东方，北面，北上。其实特豚，合升，去蹄，举肺脊二，祭肺二，鱼十有四，腊一肫，髀不升，皆饪。设扃鼏。设洗于阼阶东南，馔于房中，醯酱二豆，菹醢四豆，兼巾之。黍稷四敦，皆盖。大羹湆在爨。尊于室中北墉下，有禁，玄酒在西，绤幂，加勺，皆南枋。尊于房户之东，无玄酒。篚在南，实四爵合卺。
主人爵弁，𫄸裳缁袉。从者毕玄端，乘墨车，从车二乘，执烛前马。妇车亦如之，有裧。至于门外。主人筵于户西，西上，右几。女次，纯衣𫄸衻，立于房中，南面。姆𫄥笄宵衣，在其右。女从者毕袗玄，𫄥笄，被顈黼，在其后。主人玄端，迎于门外，西面再拜。宾东面答拜。主人揖入，宾执雁从。至于庙门，揖入。三揖，至于阶，三让。主人升，西面。宾升，北面，奠雁，再拜稽首，降，出。妇从，降自西阶。主人不降送。壻御妇车，授绥，姆辞不受。妇乘以几，姆加景，乃驱。御者代。壻乘其车先，俟于门外。
……
en:
【The Gentleman's Wedding Ceremony, Part 2】

The wedding ceremony. The groom's family sends a messenger to the bride's family with a wild goose as a betrothal gift. The host sets a mat to the west of the door, facing west, with a low table on the right. The messenger arrives in dark ceremonial robes. The usher goes out to ask his business, then enters to announce it. The host, dressed in the same attire as the guest, welcomes him outside the gate and bows twice. The guest does not return the bow. They bow to each other and enter. At the temple gate, they bow again and enter. After three bows, they reach the steps, where they yield to each other three times. The host leads the guest up, facing west. The guest ascends the western steps, and when he reaches the ridge beam, he faces east and delivers the message. The host, on the eastern steps, faces north and bows twice. The wild goose is presented between the pillars, facing south. The guest descends and leaves. The host descends and gives the wild goose to the elder steward.
The usher goes out to ask the guest to present the wild goose, and then asks for the bride's name. The host agrees. The guest enters and presents the gift as before.
The usher goes out to ask if the guest has finished his business, then enters to announce it, and goes out to invite the guest to a toast of sweet wine. The guest politely declines at first, then accepts. The host removes the low table and changes the mat, facing east, and places a jar of sweet wine with a ladle in the inner chamber. The host welcomes the guest outside the temple gate, and they bow and yield as before, then ascend. The host, facing north, bows twice. The guest, on the western steps, faces north and returns the bow. The host wipes the low table and hands it to the guest by the leg, bowing as he sends it. The guest steps aside with the table, faces north, and places it to the left of his seat on the western steps, then returns the bow. The assistant pours the sweet wine, adds a ladle with the spoon facing up, and comes out of the inner chamber. The host receives the wine, with the handle facing him, and stands before the mat facing northwest. The guest bows, receives the wine, and returns to his position. The host, on the eastern steps, bows as he sends it off. The assistant presents dried meat and pickled vegetables. The guest takes his seat on the mat, sits with the goblet in his left hand, offers the dried meat and pickles, and uses the ladle to offer the sweet wine three times. On the western steps, facing north, he sits, sips the wine, sets down the ladle, rises, sits to place the goblet, and then bows. The host returns the bow. The guest returns to the mat, places the goblet to the left of the offerings, leaves the mat, and, facing north, sits to take the dried meat. The host declines this. The guest descends, gives the dried meat to his attendant, and leaves. The host sees him off outside the gate and bows twice.
The divination for good fortune is announced, using a wild goose, following the same rites as the betrothal.
The betrothal gift is presented: dark and light silks, and a pair of deer skins, following the rites of the divination announcement.
The date of the wedding is requested, using a wild goose. The host declines at first, the guest insists, and the date is announced, following the rites of the betrothal gift.
On the wedding day, at the beginning of dusk, three cauldrons are set up outside the gate of the sleeping quarters, to the east, facing north, with the most important on the north. They contain a single suckling pig, cooked whole, with the hooves removed, two pieces of lung and spine, two pieces of lung for offerings, fourteen fish, one piece of dried meat from a whole animal, with the haunch not included, all cooked thoroughly. The cauldrons are fitted with bars and covers. A basin is placed to the southeast of the eastern steps. The food is arranged in the inner chamber: two dishes of vinegar and sauce, four dishes of pickled vegetables and meat, all covered with a cloth. Four vessels of millet and rice, all with lids. The broth for the great offering is kept at the stove. A wine jar is placed in the chamber beneath the north wall, on a stand, with dark wine to the west, covered with a coarse cloth, with a ladle, all with handles facing south. Another wine jar is placed east of the door of the inner chamber, without dark wine. A basket is to the south, containing four goblets and a gourd cup split in two.
The groom wears a dark cap and dark lower garment with black trim. His attendants are all in dark robes, riding in a dark carriage, followed by two carriages, with torchbearers leading the horses. The bride's carriage is similar, with a curtain. They arrive at the gate. The host sets a mat to the west of the door, facing west, with a low table on the right. The bride, in her chamber, wears a plain robe with a dark border, facing south. Her matron, in a dark robe with a hairpin, stands to her right. The bride's attendants are all in dark robes, with hairpins, and wear white embroidered shawls, standing behind her. The host, in dark robes, welcomes them outside the gate, facing west, and bows twice. The guest, facing east, returns the bow. The host bows and enters, and the guest follows with the wild goose. At the temple gate, they bow and enter. After three bows, they reach the steps, where they yield three times. The host ascends, facing west. The guest ascends, faces north, places the wild goose, bows twice with his head to the ground, descends, and leaves. The bride follows, descending from the western steps. The host does not descend to see her off. The groom drives the bride's carriage, hands her the reins, but the matron declines on her behalf. The bride steps onto the carriage using a stool, the matron drapes a cloak over her, and then they drive off. The groom's driver takes over. The groom rides in his own carriage ahead and waits outside the gate.

《岁时杂记》中记载，“煮豚肉，并汁露顿，候其冻取之，谓之姜豉。以荐饼而食之。或剜以匕，或裁以刀，调以姜豉，故名焉。”又有《朝野佥载》言，“唐姜晦为吏部侍郎，眼不识字，手不解书，滥掌铨衡，曾无分别。选人歌曰：‘今年选数恰相当，都由座主无文章。案后一腔冻猪肉，所以名为姜侍郎。’”
en:
This traditional dish involves slowly simmering pork until tender, then allowing the rich broth to congeal as it cools. The resulting meat aspic is sliced into neat portions and served with a tangy ginger-vinegar dipping sauce, creating a smooth, refreshing delicacy that makes a perfect drinking companion. That's not enough—Ye Xin will also offer an extra dish of pungent mustard alongside. 



The Miscellaneous Notes on Seasonal Times describes: "Pork is stewed with its broth until solidified through cold exposure, forming what we call 'ginger relish.' It's sliced with a knife or scooped with a spoon, then dressed with ginger seasoning to accompany flatbreads." The Public and Private Chronicles offers a satirical anecdote from Tang Dynasty officialdom:



During the Tang Dynasty, there was a man named Jiang Hui who served as Deputy Minister of Personnel Affairs. Yet despite his high office, he was illiterate. He was entrusted with selecting and appointing officials, though he lacked any real ability to recognize talent. Disappointed candidates composed a biting folk song to mock him: "This year's selections all went astray. The chief examiner was blind, though wide awake. Sitting stiff as a slab of frozen pork, no wonder he is called Jiang the wooden dork."

西汉武帝年间，西域有古国乌孙，不务农耕，以游牧为生，地产良马。《汉书·张骞传》记载：“骞既至乌孙，致赐谕指……乌孙发译道送骞，与乌孙使数十人，马数十匹，报谢，因令窥汉，知其广大。”张骞出使西域，将乌孙骏马带回中原，汉武帝见乌孙马神骏非凡，欣喜万分，名曰“西极”。
乌孙西极体格魁伟，四肢强健，头颅小巧，耳短眸清，外形俊秀。性温顺，耐粗放，春夏时节食草增膘，秋冬时节亦能刨雪觅食，力速兼备，挽乘皆宜，为西域特有的良马马种。
en:
The Shuowen Jiezi explains: "The character bo means a horse of impure color." Among the Wusun Western Supreme horses, those with an uneven, mottled coat were called Jinbo, or Gold Piebalds.
During the reign of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, the nomadic Wusun kingdom in the Western Regions was renowned for its excellent horses. The Book of Han records how the envoy Zhang Qian returned from his mission with Wusun steeds. Struck by their majestic grace, Emperor Wu named them "Western Supremes."
These horses are large and muscular, with sturdy limbs, small heads, and clear eyes, giving them an elegant appearance. Gentle in temperament yet hardy, they fatten on grass in spring and summer and can dig through snow for forage in winter. Combining both strength and speed, they are suited for riding and pulling alike, making them a prized breed unique to the Western Regions.

en:
Hang the white cloth outside the city for me.
Three hundred dye vats once stood in Luancheng. Now all are brimming with blood and fire. The secret formulas have gone south with the craftsmen, yet the last bolt of white cloth has come at last to this, a flag of surrender, perhaps soon to serve as my own shroud.
I am ashamed. Yesterday the court's transfer order arrived, every line stamped in vermilion to congratulate me on my promotion. So in the end, the bones of a whole city are worth no more than a single phrase in another man's mouth: losses in battle.
When the white flag is raised, I ask only that you listen to the wind. If you hear the clatter of looms, perhaps it is my wife opening a new dye shop by the Bridge of Oblivion. She always said that in her next life, she would dye the color of first dawn.
My story began with making spring garments in Luancheng, and now it ends with clothing Luancheng in mourning white.

在一个风雨浇家的夜晚，三个英熊将要迎来他们有身以来见过的最为可怕的敌人。
那人是谁？那人叫什么名字？那人为什么要来？
没人知道，谁也不知道。
世上的人只知道，那夜之后，世上少了一个大脚寨，多了一个龙虎寨。
而龙与虎，正是那三位英熊的名字。
张龙、张虎，张豹。

作者注：寨名由三位英熊投票选出，支持两票，反对一票，公正公平，并无偏私。
en:
The blade was no ordinary blade. Cutting iron was as easy as chopping wood.

The ones holding this blade were not just anybody. There were three heroes: Zhang Long, Zhang Hu, and Zhang Bao. Folks called them Dragon, Tiger, and Leopard, or the Beast Brothers. These three were famous for being strong, clever, and brave. When they joined hands, nothing could stop them.

That night, wind howled, rain smashed the ground. The three brothers stood together, waiting. The fiercest enemy arrived, but not one of them flinched. Who that enemy was, nobody remembers now. What everyone remembers is, after that night, the Big Foot Fort was gone, and Tiger Fort stood tall.

Why call it Tiger Fort? Easy. Zhang Hu, the Tiger, said, "Let's use Tiger Fort." Long, the Dragon, agreed straight away. Bao, the Leopard, wanted his own name, but two votes beat one. That's how real heroes make decisions—straight and fair.

en:
In Crosswind Bazaar stands an inn named Clearsky Tower. Its proprietress, Eleventh Lady Chu, is known across the Jianghu as "Storm's Respite." Her golden rule is absolute: no matter the blood feud, all strife must cease within her walls.
Because of this sanctuary, treasure hunters venturing into the Mistveil Forest make it their hub to rest, form parties, or trade secrets. Yet with its steep prices, many a down-on-their-luck wanderer can only nurse tea at the roadside stall outside, gazing up with envy.
Rumors swirl around the tower and its enigmatic owner. Some say Eleventh Lady Chu is the twin sister of Twelfth Brother Chu, the spymaster of the Nine Mortal Ways. Others whisper that this handsome, cross-dressing beauty shares deep ties with Velvet Shade, particularly with the Rose of the Twenty-Four Seasonal Flowers. Still others claim the Faceless Ones incident in Qinghe first reached Kaifeng through this very inn.

zh:
阿古有崽了，可它怎么都高兴不起来。
因为它不知道，在哪儿才能让崽儿顺顺利利出生。
这世道太乱，连人想要平安都办不到，何况是狗呢？
阿古一路寻来，处处不是刀剑相向，便是有高头大马的坏人在巡逻，它没办法。只好避着人继续逃。
阿古的步伐越来越沉，它知道自己走不动了。抬头一看，是一座破庙。
或许是天无绝狗之路，破庙里头，倒是比别处暖和些。
阿古选了一处地方躺倒，朦朦胧胧间，它似乎听到庙里热闹起来。
有两批穿着不同的侠客都赶在庙里，嘴里却都念叨着一个日子。
初六，初六。
阿古隐约感觉，侠客说的这个日子越来越近了，而肚子里的动静也越来越大。
或许，这个孩子会降生在初六。
en:
Maternal was pregnant, but she couldn't find any reason to be happy.
She didn't know where she could safely bring her pups into the world.
The world was in chaos; even humans couldn't find peace, let alone a dog.
Maternal traveled a long way, but everywhere she went, she found either drawn blades or fierce villains on horseback. She had no choice but to keep fleeing, avoiding everyone.
Her steps grew heavier, and she knew she couldn't go much further. Looking up, she saw a ruined temple.
Perhaps there was a way out after all; the ruined temple was warmer than anywhere else.
Maternal chose a spot to lie down. In a daze, she seemed to hear the temple grow lively.
Two groups of differently dressed swordsmen had gathered in the temple, both mentioning the same date.
The sixth, the sixth.
Maternal vaguely felt that the date the swordsmen spoke of was drawing near, and the movement in her belly grew stronger.
Perhaps this child would be born on the sixth.
